items.title: The one-body reduction trace law of the finite-mode permutation sectors
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a
complex Hilbert space of finite dimension $d\ge1$
([[def-hilbert-space]]), let $n\ge1$, let $H^{\otimes n}$ be the $n$-fold
completed tensor power with $H^{\otimes0}:=\mathbb C$, $H^{\otimes1}:=H$ and
$H^{\otimes(k+1)}:=H^{\otimes k}\widehat\otimes H$, let $(U_\pi)_{\pi\in S_n}$
be the permutation unitaries and let
$P_\sigma^{(n)}$, $\sigma\in\{+,-\}$, be the sector projections
([[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]), with sector space
$$\mathfrak H_n^\sigma:=\operatorname{ran}P_\sigma^{(n)}\subseteq H^{\otimes n}.$$
For $O\in\mathcal B(H)$ and $i\in\{1,\dots,n\}$ let $O^{(i)}\in\mathcal B(H^{\otimes n})$
be the operator of clause (a) below, and put
$$\Sigma(O):=\sum_{i=1}^n O^{(i)}\in\mathcal B(H^{\otimes n}).$$
Identify $H^{\otimes n}$ with $H\widehat\otimes H^{\otimes(n-1)}$ by the
surjective linear isometry $J_n$ of clause (b) below, and let
$\operatorname{Tr}_{H^{\otimes(n-1)}}$ be the partial trace of
[[thm-nrqm-composites-finite-partial-trace-and-schmidt]] clause (a) over the
second factor of that identification. Then:

(a) *slot operators*: for every $O\in\mathcal B(H)$ and every
$i\in\{1,\dots,n\}$ there is a unique $O^{(i)}\in\mathcal B(H^{\otimes n})$
with $O^{(i)}(v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n)=v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{i-1}\otimes Ov_i\otimes v_{i+1}\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n$
for all $v_1,\dots,v_n\in H$; it satisfies $\|O^{(i)}\|\le\|O\|$ and
$(O^*)^{(i)}=(O^{(i)})^*$; in particular $O=O^*$ gives $O^{(i)}=(O^{(i)})^*$;

(b) *parenthesisation*: the assignment
$v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n\mapsto v_1\otimes(v_2\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n)$
extends to a surjective linear isometry
$J_n:H^{\otimes n}\to H\widehat\otimes H^{\otimes(n-1)}$; for $n=1$ the
empty product is $1\in\mathbb C$ and $J_1u=u\otimes1$;

(c) *permutation invariance*: $U_\pi\,\Sigma(O)\,U_\pi^*=\Sigma(O)$ for every
$\pi\in S_n$; consequently $\Sigma(O)$ preserves both sector spaces and commutes with $P_\sigma^{(n)}$:
$$\Sigma(O)P_\sigma^{(n)}=P_\sigma^{(n)}\Sigma(O)=P_\sigma^{(n)}\Sigma(O)P_\sigma^{(n)};$$

(d) *trace law*: for every density operator $\rho$ on the sector space
$\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]
clause (a)), let $j:\mathfrak H_n^\sigma\hookrightarrow H^{\otimes n}$ be
the isometric inclusion and define its zero extension
$\widetilde\rho:=j\rho j^*\in\mathcal B(H^{\otimes n})$; then
for every $O\in\mathcal B(H)$ one has $\operatorname{tr}(\widetilde\rho\,\Sigma(O))=n\,\operatorname{tr}(\gamma\,O)$,
where $\gamma:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H^{\otimes(n-1)}}\bigl(J_n\widetilde\rho J_n^{-1}\bigr)\in\mathcal B(H)$;

(e) *the reduced operator is a density operator*: the operator $\gamma$ of
clause (d) is a density operator on $H$; it is independent of the choice of
slot in the sense that it equals the partial trace of $\widetilde\rho$ over
the other $n-1$ slots in the parenthesisation in which the retained slot is
the one the display names; for $n=1$, $\gamma=\rho$. If
$\mathfrak H_n^\sigma=\{0\}$, there is no density operator of trace one on
that sector, so clauses (d)-(e) make no assertion about a sector preparation;

(f) *scope*: clauses (a)-(e) are exact operator identities on the
finite-dimensional labelled tensor powers; no physical system, particle
species, preparation or measurement is asserted, and the parameter $n$ is a
dimension count of the construction, not an observed particle number.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 6.3.1 printed pages 125-127 (PDF pages 133-135): the reduced density operator obtained by tracing out the environment, equations (6.75)-(6.80)
G. Teschl, Topics in Real and Functional Analysis (November 17, 2017), Section 3.6 printed pages 93-98: trace-class operators, partial traces and cyclicity of the trace

items.title: Closed formulas for the two-level canonical weights, mean energy, entropy and free energy
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$\varepsilon>0$ and $\beta>0$ be real parameters, let $\mathfrak h$ be a
two-dimensional complex Hilbert space with orthonormal basis
$(u_0,u_1)$ ([[def-hilbert-space]],
[[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]),
and let $H:=T_{u_1,u_1}\varepsilon=\varepsilon\,T_{u_1,u_1}$ be the
self-adjoint operator with eigenvalues $0$ on $\mathbb Cu_0$ and
$\varepsilon$ on $\mathbb Cu_1$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]). Let
$$Z:=\sum_{j=0}^{1}e^{-\beta E_j},\qquad \rho_\beta:=\frac1Z\sum_{j=0}^{1}e^{-\beta E_j}T_{u_j,u_j},\qquad s(\rho):=-\sum_{i:\,w_i>0}w_i\log w_i$$
be the partition sum, canonical operator and entropy of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-finite-gibbs-free-energy-minimum]] clause
(a), with $E_0=0$, $E_1=\varepsilon$ and $w_i$ the eigenvalues of a density
operator $\rho$ on $\mathfrak h$ ([[def-natural-logarithm]]). Then:

(a) $Z=1+e^{-\beta\varepsilon}\in(1,2)$, and
$$\rho_\beta=\frac1Z\bigl(T_{u_0,u_0}+e^{-\beta\varepsilon}T_{u_1,u_1}\bigr)$$
is a density operator on $\mathfrak h$ that is not the maximally mixed state
$\tfrac12\mathrm{id}$;

(b) the mean energy is the exact identity
$$\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H)=\frac{\varepsilon e^{-\beta\varepsilon}}{Z}=\frac{\varepsilon}{e^{\beta\varepsilon}+1},\qquad 0<\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H)<\frac{\varepsilon}{2};$$

(c) the entropy and free energy satisfy
$$s(\rho_\beta)=\log Z+\frac{\beta\varepsilon}{e^{\beta\varepsilon}+1}=\log\bigl(1+e^{-\beta\varepsilon}\bigr)+\frac{\beta\varepsilon\,e^{-\beta\varepsilon}}{1+e^{-\beta\varepsilon}},\qquad 0\le s(\rho_\beta)<\log 2,$$
and, with $F:=-\beta^{-1}\log Z$,
$$\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H)-\beta^{-1}s(\rho_\beta)=F ;$$

(d) *scope*: clauses (a)-(c) are exact algebraic identities for the
declared two-dimensional Hilbert space and the two real parameters
$\varepsilon,\beta>0$; no temperature, thermodynamic, equilibrium or
measurement interpretation is asserted, and the parameter $\beta$ carries no
physical dimension in this lemma.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 6.4 printed pages 129-131 (PDF pages 137-139): the Gibbs distribution (6.94), the internal energy U = Tr(H rho) (6.95), the identity s = beta U + ln Z (6.97) and the entropy S = k_B s (6.98)

I. Burmistrov and A. Lunkin, Lecture Notes on Statistical Mechanics (HSE, January 10, 2023), Section 1.1.2 printed page 13: the Gibbs distribution rho = e^{-beta H}/Z with Z = Tr e^{-beta H} and the mean energy E = Tr rho H; Section 1.1.3 printed pages 13-14: the von Neumann entropy; Section 1.1.5 printed page 15: F = -T ln Z

items.title: CC realization of the bounded spatial operator on a finite-component H² domain
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Fix integers $N,M\ge1$, $a>0$, and a real measurable function $V:\mathbb R^{3N}\to\mathbb R$ with $v=\operatorname{ess\,sup}|V|<\infty$. Put
$$\mathcal H=L^2(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C^M),\qquad Y=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C^M)=H^2(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C^M),$$
where the vector space, pairing and Sobolev norm are the finite component sums of the scalar conventions of [[def-hilbert-space]], [[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]] and [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]. Use the componentwise Plancherel unitary of [[thm-plancherel]], with the negative-sign $2\pi$ convention of [[def-fourier-transform-on-l-one-of-rn]]. Define
$$w(\xi)=4\pi^2a|\xi|^2,\qquad K=\mathcal F_2^{-1}M_w\mathcal F_2,\qquad D(K)=\{u:w\mathcal F_2u\in\mathcal H\}.$$
Then $D(K)=Y$, and $Ku=-a\Delta u$ for every $u\in Y$, with the distributional Laplacian acting componentwise. The operator
$$H=K+M_V=-a\Delta+V,\qquad D(H)=Y,$$
is densely defined and self-adjoint on exactly $Y$, and $H\ge-v$. Both $K$ and $H$ have graph norms equivalent to the stated Sobolev norm, and $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C^M)$ is a core for both. For $z=\pm i\mu$ with $\mu>v$, there is the concrete two-sided inverse
$$R_H(z)=(H-z)^{-1}=R_0(z)\sum_{k\ge0}(-M_VR_0(z))^k,\qquad R_0(z)=\mathcal F_2^{-1}M_{(w-z)^{-1}}\mathcal F_2,$$
with range exactly $Y$ and $\|R_H(z)\|\le(\mu-v)^{-1}$.

This realizes the equal-mass bounded spatial operator used at fixed $N$ by setting $a=\hbar^2/(2m)$ and any finite spin multiplicity $M$; for an $N$-fold spin-$s$ tensor the full multiplicity is $M=(2s+1)^N$. The lemma makes no statement about Coulomb potentials, unequal-mass operators, thermodynamic limits, or physical assignments. It uses no Axiom of Choice or Kato–Rellich theorem.

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, bounded perturbations of the free operator; concrete CC realization proved locally here

items.title: Finite spin components of an N-fold spatial tensor product
items.statement:
**Slot convention.** For $\ell\ge1$, $S_\ell$ acts on $\{0,\dots,\ell-1\}$ as in [[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]. On one-based tuple positions use $\widehat{\pi}(k):=1+\pi(k-1)$ for $1\le k\le\ell$. Conjugation by $k\mapsto k-1$ gives $\widehat{\pi\sigma}=\widehat{\pi}\circ\widehat{\sigma}$ and $\widehat{\pi^{-1}}=\widehat{\pi}^{-1}$; thus the supplier's tensor action becomes $U_\pi(v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_\ell)=v_{\widehat{\pi}^{-1}(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{\widehat{\pi}^{-1}(\ell)}$. The parameters of $U_\pi$ and $\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)$ remain canonical zero-based permutations.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $N,r\ge1$ be integers, $H=L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^r)$, $\mathcal S_N=(\mathbb C^r)^{\otimes N}$, and $M=r^N$. In the product basis $e_a=e_{a_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{a_N}$ indexed by $a\in\{1,\dots,r\}^N$, identify $\mathcal S_N$ with $\mathbb C^M$ and write $\mathcal L_N=L^2(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C^M)$. Then:

(a) There is a unique unitary $\Theta_N:H^{\otimes N}\to\mathcal L_N$ such that
$$[\Theta_N(f_1\otimes\cdots\otimes f_N)]_a(x_1,\dots,x_N)=\prod_{j=1}^N[f_j(x_j)]_{a_j}.$$

(b) For $\pi\in S_N$, let $U_\pi$ be the permutation of the complete one-particle factors and $R_\pi e_a=e_{a_{\widehat{\pi}^{-1}(1)}}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{a_{\widehat{\pi}^{-1}(N)}}$ the permutation of spin factors. With $X^\pi=(x_{\widehat{\pi}(1)},\dots,x_{\widehat{\pi}(N)})$, the conjugate permutation is
$$\mathcal U_\pi:=\Theta_NU_\pi\Theta_N^{-1},\qquad (\mathcal U_\pi\Psi)(X)=R_\pi\Psi(X^\pi).$$
In particular $[\mathcal U_\pi\Psi]_a(X)=\Psi_{(a_{\widehat{\pi}(1)},\dots,a_{\widehat{\pi}(N)})}(X^\pi)$; averaging this combined action gives $\mathcal P_\pm=\Theta_NP_\pm^{(N)}\Theta_N^{-1}$.

(c) The component domain $\mathcal D_N=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C^M)$ is the set of tuples with every scalar component in $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C)$. If a scalar self-adjoint $T$ has this scalar domain and its domain is preserved by every spatial block permutation, commuting with that permutation on the domain, its finite direct sum $T_M\Psi=(T\Psi_a)_a$ on $\mathcal D_N$ is self-adjoint, retains every scalar lower bound $T\ge cI$, and commutes with the combined permutations on that domain. The restrictions of $T_M$ to $\operatorname{ran}\mathcal P_\pm$, with domain $\mathcal D_N\cap\operatorname{ran}\mathcal P_\pm$, are self-adjoint when the sector is nonzero; on the zero sector the unique zero operator has domain $\{0\}$.

(d) For matrices $A_j\in\mathcal B(\mathbb C^r)$, the constant spin action $A_1\otimes\cdots\otimes A_N$ preserves $\mathcal D_N$ and commutes with $T_M$. Its permutation covariance is
$$R_\pi(A_1\otimes\cdots\otimes A_N)R_\pi^{-1}=A_{\widehat{\pi}^{-1}(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes A_{\widehat{\pi}^{-1}(N)}.$$
Thus a common internal unitary $A^{\otimes N}$ commutes with $\mathcal U_\pi$, preserves both sectors and commutes with their restricted operators. This is a tensor identity and asserts no physical spin-statistics assignment. For $r=1$ all spin actions are scalar and $\Theta_N$ is the iterated scalar product unitary; for $N=1$ it is the identity component identification.

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, Section 1.4 (finite tensor products and orthogonal sums); local derivation from the declared suppliers

items.title: Fixed-particle-number occupation bases and the countable-mode partition criterion
items.statement:
**Slot convention.** For $\ell\ge1$, $S_\ell$ acts on $\{0,\dots,\ell-1\}$ as in [[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]. On one-based tuple positions use $\widehat{\pi}(k):=1+\pi(k-1)$ for $1\le k\le\ell$. Conjugation by $k\mapsto k-1$ gives $\widehat{\pi\sigma}=\widehat{\pi}\circ\widehat{\sigma}$ and $\widehat{\pi^{-1}}=\widehat{\pi}^{-1}$; thus the supplier's tensor action becomes $U_\pi(v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_\ell)=v_{\widehat{\pi}^{-1}(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{\widehat{\pi}^{-1}(\ell)}$. The parameters of $U_\pi$ and $\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)$ remain canonical zero-based permutations.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space with a supplied countably infinite orthonormal basis $(e_j)_{j\ge1}$, let $N\ge1$ be an integer, and let $\varepsilon_j\in\mathbb R$ with $\varepsilon_j\ge b$ for a fixed $b\in\mathbb R$. Use the completed tensor power and permutation-sector projections of [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]] and [[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]], and write $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma:=\operatorname{ran}P_\sigma^{(N)}$ for $\sigma\in\{+,-\}$. Then:

(a) For every finitely supported sequence $n=(n_j)_{j\ge1}$ of nonnegative integers with $\sum_jn_j=N$, put $\operatorname{orb}(n):=\{(i_1,\ldots,i_N):\#\{k:i_k=j\}=n_j\text{ for every }j\}$ and
$$b_n^+:=|\operatorname{orb}(n)|^{-1/2}\sum_{i\in\operatorname{orb}(n)}e_{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{i_N}.$$
For every $N$-element subset $J=\{j_1<\cdots<j_N\}$ of the positive integers, put
$$b_J^-:=\frac1{\sqrt{N!}}\sum_{\pi\in S_N}\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)e_{j_{\widehat{\pi}(1)}}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{j_{\widehat{\pi}(N)}}.$$
These are orthonormal bases of the symmetric and antisymmetric sectors respectively. Denote their countable index sets by $\mathcal C_N^+$ and $\mathcal C_N^-$, and write $b_c^\sigma$ for the corresponding vector. Define $E_n:=\sum_jn_j\varepsilon_j$ and $E_J:=\sum_{j\in J}\varepsilon_j$.

(b) The fixed-$N$ free energy operator is the self-adjoint diagonal operator
$$D(H_N^\sigma):=\left\{\psi=\sum_{c\in\mathcal C_N^\sigma}a_cb_c^\sigma:\sum_c|E_c|^2|a_c|^2<\infty\right\},\qquad H_N^\sigma\psi:=\sum_cE_ca_cb_c^\sigma.$$
It is bounded below by $Nb$, and is the closure of its action on finite occupation sums. On elementary tensors of modes it agrees with the restriction of the labelled energy sum $\sum_{k=1}^N\varepsilon_{i_k}$, with the same diagonal-domain closure. Its spectral PVM is
$$E_N^\sigma(B)\psi=\sum_c\mathbf1_B(E_c)a_cb_c^\sigma.$$

(c) For $\beta>0$, let $q_j:=e^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}>0$, so $q_j\le e^{-\beta b}$. Define the extended positive trace of a bounded positive operator as its nonnegative diagonal sum in the supplied occupation basis; its independence of any other supplied orthonormal basis is proved below. With this trace (allowed to be $+\infty$),
$$Z_N^+(\beta):=\operatorname{Tr}e^{-\beta H_N^+}=h_N(q):=\sum_{1\le i_1\le\cdots\le i_N}q_{i_1}\cdots q_{i_N},$$
$$Z_N^-(\beta):=\operatorname{Tr}e^{-\beta H_N^-}=e_N(q):=\sum_{1\le i_1<\cdots<i_N}q_{i_1}\cdots q_{i_N}.$$
All sums are nonnegative-series sums. For either sign,
$$\left(\prod_{k=1}^{N-1}q_k\right)\sum_{j=N}^\infty q_j\le Z_N^\sigma(\beta)\le\left(\sum_{j=1}^\infty q_j\right)^N.$$
For $N=1$ the product is $1$, the tail starts at $1$, and both partition sums equal $\sum_jq_j$. Consequently, for every fixed $N\ge1$ and either statistics,
$$0<Z_N^\sigma(\beta)<\infty\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\sum_j e^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}<\infty.$$
The bounded positive operator $e^{-\beta H_N^\sigma}$ is trace class exactly in this case, and its ordinary trace then equals the displayed occupation sum. This is a fixed-$N$ criterion, not a trace over all particle numbers.

references.title: F. H. L. Essler, Advanced Quantum Theory, Chapter 1: finite occupation configurations; the countable fixed-N extension and trace bounds are proved locally here

items.title: Spectral first moments and trace products with a density operator
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $A$ be a self-adjoint operator on a nonzero complex Hilbert space, let $E_A$ be its spectral PVM, let $\rho$ be a density operator, and set $\mu_\rho^A(B):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_A(B))$. Then:

(a) The finite first mean is defined exactly under the absolute-first-moment condition
$$\int_{\mathbb R}|a|\,d\mu_\rho^A(a)<\infty,$$
and its value is $m:=\int a\,d\mu_\rho^A(a)$. For every positive-eigenvalue expansion $\rho=\sum_kw_kT_{u_k,u_k}$ of [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] (a), with $w_k>0$ and $\sum_kw_k=1$, one has
$$\int|a|\,d\mu_\rho^A=\sum_kw_k\int|a|\,dE_{A,u_k},\qquad m=\sum_kw_k\int a\,dE_{A,u_k}.$$
The first identity allows infinity; the second is asserted under the stated integrability condition and converges absolutely. This condition does not require $u_k\in D(A)$.

(b) If $A$ is bounded, the condition in (a) holds automatically and
$$m=\operatorname{tr}(A\rho)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho A).$$

(c) Suppose the condition in (a) holds and the **literal product** $A\rho$ is defined on the whole Hilbert space and is trace class; thus $\rho(H)\subset D(A)$ and $T:=A\rho\in\mathcal S_1(H)$. Then
$$m=\operatorname{tr}(T).$$
Moreover the densely defined product $\rho A$ has bounded closure $T^*$, that closure is trace class, and $\operatorname{tr}(\overline{\rho A})=m$. This is a conditional trace identity for defined trace-class products. The existence of the mean alone does not assert any of these unbounded-operator product hypotheses.

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, Chapters 2-3: density eigenexpansions and spectral integrals; the typed-product comparison is proved locally here

items.title: The declared fixed-N many-body model: species sector, one-particle data, interaction and the sector energy observable
items.statement:
**Slot convention.** For $\ell\ge1$, $S_\ell$ acts on $\{0,\dots,\ell-1\}$ as in [[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]. On one-based tuple positions use $\widehat{\pi}(k):=1+\pi(k-1)$ for $1\le k\le\ell$. Conjugation by $k\mapsto k-1$ gives $\widehat{\pi\sigma}=\widehat{\pi}\circ\widehat{\sigma}$ and $\widehat{\pi^{-1}}=\widehat{\pi}^{-1}$; thus the supplier's tensor action becomes $U_\pi(v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_\ell)=v_{\widehat{\pi}^{-1}(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{\widehat{\pi}^{-1}(\ell)}$. The parameters of $U_\pi$ and $\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)$ remain canonical zero-based permutations.

**(a) Adopted readings, units and choice hypotheses.** Adopt the state and
composition postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1), the
observable and probability postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2), the
autonomous-dynamics postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]
(P4), the non-relativistic kinematics postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]] (P5)
and the identical-particle and spin postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]] (P6), in the state
reading of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], the observable
reading of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], the
evolution reading of [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] and
the sector vocabulary of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]].
P5 and the massive spin-$s$ reading below apply to the full spatial space
$H_s=L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^{2s+1})$. In the finite-mode branch,
clause (b)(ii) explicitly replaces P5's full-space state and Hamiltonian
assignments (iii),(iv) by retained-space assignments: P1, P2 and P4 are
read on that retained space, P6(i) gives its permutation sectors, and
P6(ii) still specifies spin on $H_s$, with no automatic full spin
representation on the retained space. This is an additional model
idealization, not a consequence of P5.
Let the species parameters mass $m>0$
(kg), spin label $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\dots\}$ and statistics choice
$\sigma\in\{+,-\}$ be given in the vocabulary of that definition and let
$H$ be the one-particle space of the chosen branch below. Use the sector
and preparation constructions of that definition (c)-(e) on $H$; fix an integer
$N\ge1$ and let $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma=\operatorname{ran}P_\sigma^{(N)}\subseteq
H^{\otimes N}$ be the declared $N$-particle sector. All quantities below are
read in the SI conventions and units of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] (energies in joules). Assume the
Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). AC is inherited from the adopted general spectral
observable and evolution interfaces of P2 and P4 and the operator suppliers
of P5; it is also required by the Coulomb realization in clause (d)(ii).
The bounded spatial operator construction in clause (d)(i) itself uses only
Countable Choice. Adopt [[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]
(P7) for the qualified apparatus and parameter identifications below.

**(b) Declared one-particle data.** The model declares a one-particle
**energy operator** in one of the two following realizations.

(i) *Spatial realization.* The one-particle space is
$H=L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^{2s+1})$ and, with $\hbar>0$ the reduced Planck
constant, the model declares a **kinetic operator** $K_1:=-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\Delta$
on $L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^{2s+1})$ and a real, measurable, bounded
**external potential** $V_{\mathrm{ext}}:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$ of essential
supremum $\|V_{\mathrm{ext}}\|_\infty<\infty$; the declared one-particle
operator is $h:=K_1+V_{\mathrm{ext}}(Q)$, self-adjoint by [[lem-nrqm-many-body-cc-bounded-spatial-realization]] with $N=1$, $M=2s+1$ and $a_1=\hbar^2/(2m)$, with domain
$W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^{2s+1})$. The particular singular external potential $V_{\mathrm{ext}}^b-g/|x|$ is included in the Coulomb branch of clause (c)(ii), whose one-particle $h$ is specified there using the $N=1$ instance of clause (d)(ii). Any other more singular declared $V_{\mathrm{ext}}$ requires a separately supplied self-adjoint realization before its operator is read as an observable.

(ii) *Finite-mode realization.* A finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space
$K$ of dimension $d\ge1$ with a declared orthonormal basis
$(f_1,\dots,f_d)$ ([[def-hilbert-space]]) is declared together with a
self-adjoint **one-particle operator** $h\in\mathcal B(K)$
([[def-bounded-linear-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]).
Also declare an orthonormal family $(g_1,\dots,g_d)$ in the full spatial
spin space $H_s$ of [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]]
clause (a). Define the **retained-mode isometry**, its adjoint, and its
orthogonal projection by
$$J:K\to H_s,\qquad J\Bigl(\sum_{j=1}^dc_jf_j\Bigr)=\sum_{j=1}^dc_jg_j,\qquad J^*\psi=\sum_{j=1}^d\langle\psi,g_j\rangle f_j,\qquad R:=JJ^*.$$
Thus $J^*J=I_K$, $R^2=R=R^*$ and
$\operatorname{ran}R=\operatorname{span}\{g_1,\dots,g_d\}$; inner products
are linear in the first variable. Here $H=K$ is the effective one-particle
space, and $\psi\in K$ represents the retained full-space vector $J\psi$.
The tensor map $J_N:=J^{\otimes N}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]] is an isometry and satisfies
$J_NU_\pi^K=U_\pi^{H_s}J_N$: the two sides agree on elementary tensors
by the slot convention and hence on the completion. The finite projection
sums consequently give $J_NP_\sigma^{(N),K}=P_\sigma^{(N),H_s}J_N$.
The retained sector is therefore isometrically embedded in the full
species sector, preserving its statistics choice.

The internal spin matrices and rotations of P6(ii) act on $H_s$.
Their restrictions are assigned on $K$ only when they preserve
$\operatorname{ran}J$; for example a full internal rotation action on $K$
requires $(I\otimes D_s(A))\operatorname{ran}J=\operatorname{ran}J$ for
every $A\in SU(2)$, with $D_s$ exactly as in P6(ii), and is then read as
$J^*(I\otimes D_s(A))J$. No such invariance is imposed here, so $d$ need
not be a multiple of $2s+1$: one retained spinor mode for $s=1/2$ is
permitted without identifying $K$ with the full two-dimensional spin
factor. P5's full-space position, momentum and commutation relations
are not asserted on $K$. The finite operator $h$ and pair operator $W$
of clause (c)(i) are independently adopted effective energy data; no
compression of a spatial Hamiltonian, equality with its evolution,
or approximation error bound is asserted. Identifying the retained modes
and these energy data with a laboratory preparation is a tested
identification with uncertainty under P7, not part of the mathematical
embedding.

**(c) Declared interaction.** The model declares a **pair interaction** in the
matching realization.

(i) *Bounded interaction.* In the spatial realization let
$W:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$ be real, measurable, bounded with
$W(-z)=W(z)$ for almost every $z$ and $\|W\|_\infty<\infty$. In the
finite-mode realization let $W\in\mathcal B(K\widehat\otimes K)$ be
self-adjoint with $U_{(0\,1)}WU_{(0\,1)}=W$, where $U_{(0\,1)}$ is the exchange
unitary of [[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]] clause (a)
in the tensor square $\widehat{K\otimes K}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]. The interaction strength
constants entering $W$ are empirical model parameters with their uncertainties
in the sense of P6 clause (iii).

(ii) *Coulomb interaction.* In the spatial realization the model may declare $W(z):=\kappa/|z|$ with a real coupling $\kappa\in\mathbb R$ in $\mathrm J\,\mathrm m$ (repulsive for $\kappa>0$). Retain a real bounded measurable external term $V_{\mathrm{ext}}^b$ as in clause (b)(i), and permit the additional singular term $-g/|x|$, where $g\in\mathbb R$ is also in $\mathrm J\,\mathrm m$, so each distance denominator in metres gives an energy in joules; the total external potential is $V_{\mathrm{ext}}^b(x)-g/|x|$. In this branch the declared one-particle operator is $h=K_1+M_{V_{\mathrm{ext}}^b-g/|x|}$ on $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^{2s+1})$, including the singular external term. Its self-adjointness and lower bound are the $N=1$ finite-component instance of clause (d)(ii), with no pair term. Thus the bounded one-particle reading in clause (b)(i) is replaced by this supplied Coulomb reading, rather than leaving the singular external term solely in $H_{\mathrm{lab}}$. The pair interaction still consists only of $\kappa/|x_i-x_j|$. The declared scalar potential on $\mathbb R^{3N}$ is
$$V(X)=V_b(X)+V_C(X),\qquad V_b(X)=\sum_{i=1}^NV_{\mathrm{ext}}^b(x_i),\qquad V_C(X)=-g\sum_{i=1}^N\frac1{|x_i|}+\kappa\sum_{1\le i<j\le N}\frac1{|x_i-x_j|}.$$
The cases $g=0$, $\kappa=0$, $V_{\mathrm{ext}}^b=0$ and either sign of either coupling are allowed. Singular values on their null collision sets are irrelevant to the multiplier classes. The singular part is supplied by [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fixed-n-coulomb-self-adjointness]]; the bounded external addition is included by the exact-domain argument in clause (d)(ii), rather than attributed to a source statement which contains only the singular sum.

**(d) The labelled energy operator and its sector restriction.** Fix the
particle masses $m_1=\cdots=m_N=m$ of the declared species.

(i) *Spatial, bounded case.* Put $r_s:=2s+1$, $\mathcal S_N:=(\mathbb C^{r_s})^{\otimes N}$ and $M:=r_s^N$. The finite product spin basis identifies $\mathcal S_N$ with $\mathbb C^M$. Use the full finite-component product unitary
$$\Theta_N:H^{\otimes N}\longrightarrow L^2(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C^M),\qquad [\Theta_N(f_1\otimes\cdots\otimes f_N)]_a(X)=\prod_{j=1}^N[f_j(x_j)]_{a_j},$$
where $a\in\{1,\dots,r_s\}^N$. Its construction and combined spatial/spin permutation action are proved in [[lem-nrqm-many-body-finite-spin-product-identification]], from the finite-component extension of [[lem-nrqm-composites-euclidean-l2-product-unitary]]. For $V(X)=\sum_iV_{\mathrm{ext}}(x_i)+\sum_{i<j}W(x_i-x_j)$ define $H_{\mathrm{lab}}=-\hbar^2\Delta_X/(2m)+M_V$ componentwise. The CC-only [[lem-nrqm-many-body-cc-bounded-spatial-realization]], with $a_i=\hbar^2/(2m)$ and component count $M$, supplies self-adjointness on
$$D(H_{\mathrm{lab}})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C^M)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C)\otimes \mathcal S_N,$$
and the lower bound $-\|V\|_\infty$. Equal masses, identical external potentials and the even pair potential make the scalar domain and operator invariant under spatial block permutations. The finite-component lemma shows that the combined permutations $\mathcal U_\pi=\Theta_NU_\pi\Theta_N^{-1}$ also permute the spin slots and commute with $H_{\mathrm{lab}}$ on its domain. Thus $\mathcal P_\sigma:=\Theta_NP_\sigma^{(N)}\Theta_N^{-1}$ reduces the operator by [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-permutation-restricted-self-adjointness]] (a)-(d), and the transported sector energy is
$$H_N^{\sigma,\mathrm{coord}}:=H_{\mathrm{lab}}\big|_{D(H_{\mathrm{lab}})\cap\operatorname{ran}\mathcal P_\sigma}.$$
It is self-adjoint on $\operatorname{ran}\mathcal P_\sigma=\Theta_N\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$, with the zero operator on the zero-sector branch. The model's tensor reading is $H_N^\sigma:=\Theta_N^{-1}H_N^{\sigma,\mathrm{coord}}\Theta_N$ on $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$. Every constant spin action commutes with the spin-independent labelled operator; a common spin unitary $A^{\otimes N}$ preserves each identical-particle sector by the finite-component lemma. For $s=0$, $M=1$ and this is the scalar product reading; for $N=1$, $M=2s+1$ and it is the one-particle component reading.

(ii) *Spatial Coulomb case.* Put $r=2s+1$, $\mathcal S_N=(\mathbb C^r)^{\otimes N}$ and $M=r^N$. Use the full spin-product unitary $\Theta_N:(L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^r))^{\otimes N}\to L^2(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C^M)$ of [[lem-nrqm-many-body-finite-spin-product-identification]] (a),(b), including its combined spatial/internal permutation action. To apply the literal Fourier normalization of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fixed-n-coulomb-self-adjointness]], choose in that mathematical theorem the masses $\widetilde m_i=m/(4\pi^2)$, its parameter $\hbar$ unchanged, one fixed center at zero, coefficients $z_{i1}=-g$ and $z_{ij}=\kappa$. The mathematical masses here are substitution parameters used to realize the already declared kinetic operator; the physical species mass remains $m$. The source kinetic symbol becomes $4\pi^2\hbar^2|\xi|^2/(2m)$, so its scalar operator is exactly
$$T_C=-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\Delta_X+V_C(X),\qquad D(T_C)=H^2(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C).$$
By the source's clauses (b),(c), $T_C$ and its finite-component extension are self-adjoint on these exact domains and bounded below for all stated real $g,\kappa$. The real bounded multiplier $M_{V_b}$ has norm at most $N\|V_{\mathrm{ext}}^b\|_\infty$, hence relative bound zero with respect to $T_C$ and to its finite-component extension. The canonical [[thm-kato-rellich]] makes
$$H_{\mathrm{lab}}=-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\Delta_X+V_C+V_b,\qquad D(H_{\mathrm{lab}})=H^2(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C^M),$$
self-adjoint on exactly this domain and bounded below; if the singular operator has lower bound $c_C$, the sum has lower bound $c_C-N\|V_{\mathrm{ext}}^b\|_\infty$. Equal masses, identical external slots and pair-independent signed coefficient $\kappa$ make the scalar operator invariant under spatial permutations. These permutations preserve $H^2$ by permuting the weak-derivative coordinates; the constant internal tensor permutations preserve the finite-component domain too. Consequently the combined projections $\mathcal P_\sigma=\Theta_NP_\sigma^{(N)}\Theta_N^{-1}$ reduce $H_{\mathrm{lab}}$, and [[lem-nrqm-many-body-finite-spin-product-identification]] (c) gives self-adjointness of its restriction on the exact domain $H^2\cap\operatorname{ran}\mathcal P_\sigma$. The declared sector energy is this restriction transported back by $\Theta_N^{-1}$ to $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$, with the unique zero-space operator when that sector is zero. This Coulomb construction uses AC in addition to the inherited framework choice hypotheses of clause (a).

(iii) *Finite-mode case.* On $K^{\otimes N}$ put
$$H_{\mathrm{lab}}:=\sum_{i=1}^N h^{(i)}+\sum_{1\le i<j\le N}W^{(ij)},$$
where $h^{(i)}$ is the slot operator of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]] (the identity on all factors but
the $i$-th, $h$ on the $i$-th) and $W^{(ij)}$ is the transport of
$W\in\mathcal B(K\widehat\otimes K)$ to the pair of slots $(i,j)$ by any
canonical permutation $\pi$ whose transported map $\widehat{\pi}$ moves that pair to the first two slots; the symmetry
$U_{(0\,1)}WU_{(0\,1)}=W$ makes the order of the pair immaterial and
$W\otimes I$ commutes with permutations fixing the first two slots, so the
transported operator is independent of the permutation chosen. Then
$H_{\mathrm{lab}}$ is bounded and self-adjoint,
it commutes with every permutation unitary, and the model's sector energy
operator is $H_N^\sigma:=H_{\mathrm{lab}}|_{\mathfrak H_N^\sigma}=P_\sigma^{(N)}H_{\mathrm{lab}}P_\sigma^{(N)}|_{\mathfrak H_N^\sigma}$.

**(e) The model's energy reading and evolution.** In every realization with
$\mathfrak H_N^\sigma\ne\{0\}$, the pair $(H_N^\sigma,\mathrm J)$ is declared to be the **assigned energy
observable** of the $N$-particle sector in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a): its
outcome law in a declared sector preparation $\rho$ is the law
$\mu^{H_N^\sigma}_\rho(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_{H_N^\sigma}(B))$ of that
definition clause (b), and its spectral data are those of the self-adjoint
operator constructed in clause (d). The **model evolution** is the unitary
flow $U(t)=\exp(-itH_N^\sigma/\hbar)$ of
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clause (b) with this
generator. If $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma=\{0\}$, clause (d) retains the unique
zero-space operator only as mathematical bookkeeping: every operator on this
space has trace zero, so there is no trace-one preparation, no assigned
physical energy observable and no preparation evolution under P1-P4.
The identification of the operator with the energy of a concrete
sample, and the assignment of numerical masses, couplings and potentials to a
laboratory species, are tested identifications with uncertainty under P7;
they are not consequences of P1-P6.

**(f) The non-interacting reading.** The model is called **non-interacting**
when $W=0$ (equivalently $\kappa=0$ only in the Coulomb branch of clause (c)(ii)), so that
$H_{\mathrm{lab}}=\sum_{i=1}^Nh^{(i)}$; in the spatial realization this is the
case of the external potential summed over slots of the stated bounded or Coulomb realization.

**(g) Scope.** The declared model is a kinematic and dynamical input of this
pair: on a nonzero sector it fixes a state space, a sector, an energy operator
and an evolution; a zero sector carries only the mathematical convention of
clause (e). It asserts no stability of matter, no Hunziker-van
Winter-Zhislin threshold statement, no statement about excited threshold
structure, no thermodynamic limit, no equilibration or thermalization, no
measured energy and no identification of its parameters with a particular
laboratory sample beyond the tested identifications of P7. The finite-mode
realization is the retained-space idealization of clause (b)(ii), with
independently assigned finite energy data and no claimed accuracy relative
to spatial evolution; the spatial realization is an idealization of an $N$-particle
non-relativistic sample with the declared external field and pair interaction.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Sections 6.1 and 10.1-10.2 printed pages 104-111 and 226-235 (PDF pages 112-119 and 234-243): composite systems, the non-interacting composite Hamiltonian, the antisymmetric electron-pair wavefunction and the two-electron Hamiltonian with the mutual electrostatic repulsion term (10.24a)

F. H. L. Essler, Advanced Quantum Theory (Oxford lecture notes, 2017/18), Chapter 1 Sections 1.1, 1.2 and 1.4 pp. 3-13: systems of independent particles, the occupation-number representation, Fock space and the second-quantised form of one- and two-body operators (equations (46)-(48) and Section 1.4.3)

items.physical_scope: The declared fixed-N many-body model of the framework: a declared species sector of P6, a declared one-particle energy operator (spatial massive-model or explicitly retained finite-mode realization), a declared pair interaction (bounded or Coulomb), the labelled energy operator and its self-adjoint restriction to the adopted symmetric or antisymmetric N-particle sector, read on nonzero sectors as the model's assigned energy observable and generator of P4 evolution; zero sectors are mathematical bookkeeping with no preparation or physical observable assignment. Finite modes are embedded in the full spatial spin space, while their energy and dynamics are separately adopted effective inputs; full spatial kinematics and spin rotations are not automatically assigned on the retained space. The model is an adopted kinematic-dynamical input of the pair; it asserts no stability of matter, no Hunziker-van Winter-Zhislin threshold statement, no thermodynamic limit, no thermalization and no identification with a laboratory sample, and every interaction constant is an empirical model parameter with uncertainty.

items.title: The declared one-body reduced operator and the one-body readout of a sector preparation
items.statement:
**(a) Adopted readings.** Adopt the state and composition postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1) and the observable and
probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2)
in the state reading of
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]] and the observable reading
of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]. Work in the
**finite-mode realization** of a declared species sector of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]]:
the one-particle space is a finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space $K$ of
dimension $d\ge1$ with its declared orthonormal modes $(f_1,\dots,f_d)$, and
the $N$-particle sector space is
$\mathfrak H_N^\sigma=\operatorname{ran}P_\sigma^{(N)}\subseteq K^{\otimes N}$
with the declared sector preparations of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-orbital-occupation-model]]. Assume
the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]).

**(b) The one-body reduced operator.** Let $\rho$ be a declared sector
preparation, that is, a density operator on $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a)).
The **one-body reduced preparation** of $\rho$ is the density operator
$\gamma_\rho$ on $K$ of clause (e) of
[[lem-nrqm-many-body-one-body-reduction-trace-law]] (with $H:=K$, $n:=N$ and
the same sector projections). Explicitly, for the sector inclusion $j$ put $\widetilde\rho=j\rho j^*$ on $K^{\otimes N}$, and for the regrouping unitary $J_N:K^{\otimes N}\to K\widehat\otimes K^{\otimes(N-1)}$ put $\gamma_\rho=\operatorname{Tr}_{K^{\otimes(N-1)}}(J_N\widetilde\rho J_N^{-1})$. Here $K^{\otimes0}=\mathbb C$, so $N=1$ gives $\gamma_\rho=\rho$. A zero sector has no preparation and makes this clause vacuous. By that lemma $\gamma_\rho$ is a density operator
on $K$ independent of which factor is traced, and for every
$O\in\mathcal B(K)$ the pairings are related by
$$\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\widetilde\rho\,\Sigma(O)\bigr)=N\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\gamma_\rho\,O\bigr),$$
where $\widetilde\rho$ is the zero extension of $\rho$ and $\Sigma(O)$ is the
sum over the $N$ labelled slots of the slot operator $O^{(i)}$.

**(c) The one-body readout.** For a declared **bounded self-adjoint**
$O\in\mathcal B(K)$ with a declared unit $u_O$ in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]], the model reads the sector
operator
$$A_O:=\Sigma(O)|_{\mathfrak H_N^\sigma}=P_\sigma^{(N)}\Sigma(O)P_\sigma^{(N)}|_{\mathfrak H_N^\sigma}$$
as an **assigned sharp observable** $(A_O,u_O)$ in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a): it
is bounded and self-adjoint on the nonzero sector space and its outcome law
in a declared sector preparation $\rho$ is the law
$\mu^{A_O}_\rho(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_{A_O}(B))$ of clause (b) of that
definition. The **one-body readout** of $O$ in $\rho$ is the mean of that law
when it exists.

**(d) Scope.** The reduced preparation $\gamma_\rho$ is a mathematical
partial trace of the sector state; it is not asserted to be the state of any
individual particle, and it does not determine the sector preparation $\rho$:
many sector preparations have the same one-body reduction. The definition
asserts no separability or factorization of $\rho$, no result for the spatial
(infinite-dimensional) realization, whose reduction would require the
separable partial trace, and no measurement of individual particle labels,
which are mathematical factor labels by P6 clause (i). Whether a declared
laboratory preparation realizes a sector preparation $\rho$ and a quantity
realizes the pair $(A_O,u_O)$ are tested identifications with uncertainty
under P7, not consequences of this definition.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Sections 6.1-6.3 printed pages 105-126 (PDF pages 113-134): composite systems, local operators A tensor I, the reduced density operator obtained by tracing out one factor, and its use for local predictions
F. H. L. Essler, Advanced Quantum Theory (Oxford lecture notes, 2017/18), Section 1.4.2 pp. 8-10: single-particle operators (46)-(48) as sums of slot operators in the occupation-number representation

items.physical_scope: The declared one-body reduction of a sector preparation in the framework's finite-mode realization: the reduced preparation on the one-particle mode space, the sector operator that sums a declared bounded one-particle quantity over the labels, and the reading of that sum as an assigned sharp observable. The reduction is a mathematical partial trace of a sector state; it asserts no physical single-particle state, no separability of the sector preparation, no measurement of an individual particle and no fact about a laboratory sample.

items.title: Entropy, the Boltzmann constant and the free-energy functional of the declared finite-sector model
items.statement:
**(a) Adopted readings and restricted sector class.** Adopt the observable and
probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2)
and the autonomous-dynamics postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]] (P4), in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]], for the declared
fixed-$N$ model of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-declared-fixed-n-model]]. This definition
applies to the class of declared models whose sector space
$\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$ is **finite-dimensional**, in particular to every
finite-mode realization
([[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-orbital-occupation-model]]), where
$D:=\dim\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$ is finite (and may be zero) by
[[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-finite-mode-occupation-counts]] clauses (a),
(b). Write $\mathcal D(\mathfrak H_N^\sigma)$ for the set of declared sector
preparations, that is, the density operators on $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a)).
If $D=0$, the only operator has trace zero, so
$\mathcal D(\mathfrak H_N^\sigma)=\varnothing$. The partition trace is
$Z_N=0$, and there is no normalized canonical density or equilibrium free
energy; $\log D$, $D^{-1}\mathrm{id}$ and $\log Z_N$ are not used in this
branch. Clauses (b), (d) and (e) below apply when $D\ge1$; the assigned
parameters of (c) can still be declared when $D=0$.
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]).

**(b) Dimensionless entropy.** For $\rho\in\mathcal D(\mathfrak H_N^\sigma)$
with eigenvalues $w_1,\dots,w_D\ge0$ (counted with multiplicity, in any
order), the **entropy** of $\rho$ is
$$s(\rho):=-\sum_{i:\,w_i>0}w_i\log w_i\in[0,\log D],$$
the quantity of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-finite-gibbs-free-energy-minimum]]
clause (a) with $\log$ the natural logarithm
([[def-natural-logarithm]]). It is dimensionless, is a function of the
eigenvalue multiset of $\rho$ alone, and equals zero exactly for pure
preparations; by clause (c) of the cited theorem $s(\rho)=\log D$ holds
exactly when $\rho=D^{-1}\mathrm{id}$.

**(c) Boltzmann constant, temperature and inverse temperature.** The model
assigns a positive **Boltzmann constant** $k_B$ and a positive **temperature**
$T$; in the SI conventions of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] the unit of $k_B$ is
$\mathrm J\,\mathrm K^{-1}$, the unit of $T$ is the kelvin, and
$$k_B=1.380\,649\times10^{-23}\ \mathrm J\,\mathrm K^{-1}$$
fixed exactly by the BIPM SI definition. The model declares the **inverse
temperature** $\beta:=1/(k_BT)$, a positive real number in $\mathrm J^{-1}$.
The value and exactness of $k_B$ are unit-convention facts; the assignment of
the parameter $T$ to a physical sample, and the identification of
$\beta=1/(k_BT)$ with an inverse thermodynamic temperature, are adopted
assumptions of the ensemble model of this pair, not consequences of P1-P4,
and are tested identifications with uncertainty under the preparation and
apparatus postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]] (P7),
whose clauses (i), (iii) and (iv) require a declared comparison and
calibration model and qualifications for measured inputs. No thermometer,
calibration or measured temperature is supplied here.

**(d) Physical entropy.** The **physical entropy** of $\rho$ is
$$S(\rho):=k_B\,s(\rho),$$
read in $\mathrm J\,\mathrm K^{-1}$. It is nonnegative, is at most
$k_B\log D$, and vanishes exactly for pure preparations.

**(e) Free-energy functional.** For $\rho\in\mathcal D(\mathfrak H_N^\sigma)$,
let $\operatorname{tr}(\rho H_N^\sigma)\in\mathbb R$ be the mean of the
declared energy observable in $\rho$ (finite because $D<\infty$, in the
moment reading of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (e)).
The **Helmholtz free-energy reading** of $\rho$ is
$$F(\rho):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho H_N^\sigma)-k_BT\,s(\rho),$$
read in joules; it is the quantity
$\operatorname{tr}(\rho H)-\beta^{-1}s(\rho)$ of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-finite-gibbs-free-energy-minimum]] clause (a)
at the identified $\beta$. For the canonical operator
$\rho_\beta:=e^{-\beta H_N^\sigma}/Z_N$ and
$Z_N:=\operatorname{tr}e^{-\beta H_N^\sigma}\in(0,\infty)$ (positive finite sum in the
nonzero finite-dimensional sector), the number $F_{\mathrm{eq}}:=-\beta^{-1}\log Z_N$
is called the **equilibrium free energy**; it is the value of the functional
at $\rho_\beta$ by the cited theorem.

**(f) Scope.** This definition covers only declared models with
finite-dimensional sector space, with the zero-sector branch of (a), and preparations in
$\mathcal D(\mathfrak H_N^\sigma)$. For a declared spatial realization, whose
sector space is infinite-dimensional, the operator $\rho\log\rho$ need not be
trace class; no entropy, physical entropy or free energy is defined here for
that case, and a separate trace-class statement would be required. The
definition asserts no increase of entropy in time, no equilibration to
$\rho_\beta$, no thermodynamic limit, no pressure or volume variable, and no
measured temperature, entropy or free energy.

references.title: BIPM, The International System of Units (SI), 9th edition 2019, Section 2.2 Table 1 printed pages 123-124 (PDF pages 12-13): the Boltzmann constant k is fixed to 1.380 649 x 10^-23 J K^-1 as an exact defining constant

J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 6.3.2 printed pages 127-129 (PDF pages 135-137): the Shannon entropy s = -sum p_i ln p_i and its operator form -Tr(rho ln rho); Section 6.4 printed pages 129-131 (PDF pages 137-139): the Gibbs distribution, beta = 1/(k_B T), the thermodynamic entropy S = k_B s (6.98) and the Helmholtz free energy F = -k_B T ln Z (6.99)

I. Burmistrov and A. Lunkin, Lecture Notes on Statistical Mechanics (HSE, January 10, 2023), Section 1.1.3 printed pages 13-14: the von Neumann entropy S = -sum_j lambda_j ln lambda_j; Section 1.1.5 printed page 15: F = -T ln Z and F = E - T S

items.physical_scope: The framework's reading of entropy and free energy for a declared fixed-N model whose sector space is finite-dimensional (the finite-mode realization): the dimensionless von Neumann entropy of a declared preparation, the assigned Boltzmann constant with its exact SI value, an assigned temperature and inverse temperature, the physical entropy in J K^-1 and the Helmholtz free-energy functional in joules. The identification beta = 1/(k_B T) and the constancy of k_B are adopted model and unit-convention assumptions; the definition asserts no increase of entropy, no equilibration, no thermodynamic limit and no measured temperature or entropy.

items.title: The canonical equilibrium-ensemble assumption: the Gibbs preparation of a declared model at assigned temperature
items.statement:
**(a) Adopted readings and framework data.** Adopt the state and composition
postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1), the observable
and probability postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2), the
autonomous-dynamics postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]
(P4) and the preparation and apparatus postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]] (P7), together with the
Boltzmann-constant and temperature conventions of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]]. Declare one of the
following model readings of the same **adopted Gibbs assignment**:

(i) a fixed-$N$ model of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-declared-fixed-n-model]], on its sector space,
with Gibbs generator $G:=H_N^\sigma$; or

(ii) a separately declared number-variable mode model, such as a one-mode
bosonic Fock space, a fermionic occupation space, or a declared countable
independent-mode space, with its declared assigned observables and energy
operator $H$. The model declares a self-adjoint Gibbs generator $G$ on that
space: either $G=H$, or a separately supplied self-adjoint realization of the
effective generator $G=H-\mu\mathcal N$, where $\mathcal N$ is the declared
particle-number operator and $\mu\in\mathbb R$ is an assigned chemical
potential in joules. The subtraction is an operator with its supplied domain,
not an assertion that a formal unbounded difference is self-adjoint.

In either reading assume $G$ is bounded below and give its spectral PVM
$E_G$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]],
[[def-projection-valued-measure]]). Let $T>0$ be an assigned temperature in
kelvin and let $\beta:=1/(k_BT)$ in $\mathrm J^{-1}$ with the assigned
Boltzmann constant $k_B$. The Gibbs assignment to either model, and the
chemical-potential identification in (ii), are additional physical
preparation assumptions made here; they are not derived from P1-P4 or from
the fixed-$N$ construction. In (ii) no restriction on the assigned real
$\mu$ is imposed beyond the declared generator and trace existence
conditions; the mode-specific convergence conditions are proved separately.
For reading (ii), $G$ specifies the Gibbs weights. If the assigned autonomous
dynamics is generated by $H$, stationarity of the Gibbs density requires its
separate dynamical or commutation hypotheses; this assignment does not
identify $H-\mu\mathcal N$ with the physical evolution generator.
The physical Helmholtz free-energy vocabulary of the entropy definition
continues to apply only to its stated nonzero finite-sector class and is not
extended to every effective generator by this postulate.
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of
the spectral calculus.

**(b) Existence hypothesis and the Gibbs preparation.** The model assumes
that the **partition trace is strictly positive and finite**:
$$0<Z:=\operatorname{Tr}e^{-\beta G}<\infty,$$
where $\operatorname{Tr}B:=\sum_{f\in\mathcal B}\langle Bf,f\rangle$ for a
bounded positive $B$ and an orthonormal basis $\mathcal B$, with value allowed
to be $+\infty$. Such a basis exists under the declared AC by the maximal
orthonormal-family argument using [[thm-zorn]] and the zero-complement
criterion of [[thm-parseval-equivalences-for-a-complete-orthonormal-family]].
This trace is basis independent: for $C:=B^{1/2}$ of
[[thm-positive-square-root]], the defining sum is
$\sum_{f\in\mathcal B}\|Cf\|^2$, whose invariance is
[[thm-hilbert-schmidt-norm-is-basis-independent]]. When the sum is finite,
$C$ is Hilbert-Schmidt ([[def-hilbert-schmidt-operator]]), so $B=C^2$ is
trace class by [[thm-trace-class-iff-product-of-two-hilbert-schmidt-operators]],
and its ordinary trace is this same diagonal sum by
[[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]. Apply this to the bounded positive operator $e^{-\beta G}$, since the
declared Gibbs generator $G$ is bounded below. The model
adopts as the **canonical** or **Gibbs preparation** of the declared model
at temperature $T$ the density operator
$$\rho_\beta:=Z^{-1}e^{-\beta G}.$$
If the sector is zero-dimensional, its partition trace is $Z=0$, no
trace-one density exists, and no canonical density or equilibrium free
energy is assigned. On a nonzero finite-dimensional model space, $Z$ is a
positive finite sum $\sum_je^{-\beta E_j}$ over the eigenvalues of $G$; no energy
sign restriction is needed. There $\rho_\beta$ is the canonical operator of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-finite-gibbs-free-energy-minimum]], and the
strict positivity and finiteness hypothesis is automatic. In reading (i),
$Z=Z_N$ and this is precisely the finite-sector Gibbs assignment.

Outside the finite-dimensional class the existence hypothesis is a genuine
restriction. For a declared non-interacting fixed-$N$ model with a supplied
countably infinite orthonormal eigenmode basis and real mode energies
$\varepsilon_j$ bounded below, the complete construction and trace criterion
of [[lem-nrqm-many-body-fixed-n-countable-mode-partition-criterion]] give
$Z_N=h_N(q)$ for bosonic statistics or $Z_N=e_N(q)$ for fermionic statistics,
where $q_j=e^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}$ and $h_N,e_N$ are the corresponding
nonnegative occupation-series sums. For every fixed $N\ge1$, either trace is
finite exactly when $\sum_jq_j<\infty$. This is a trace on the fixed-$N$
sector and permits negative mode energies.

For the separately declared full bosonic Fock models of reading (ii),
the single-mode calculation of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-single-mode-thermal-trace]] and the product
criterion of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-countable-mode-product-criterion]]
provide the separate mathematical full-Fock traces, with their original
positive mode-energy hypotheses: they sum over every particle number,
including the vacuum, giving $(1-e^{-\beta\varepsilon})^{-1}$ for one mode
and $\prod_j(1-e^{-\beta\varepsilon_j})^{-1}$ for countably many modes.
Their physical Gibbs reading is the additional assignment of (a)(ii), not a
consequence of a mathematical trace formula. Those full-Fock traces are not
substituted for the fixed-$N$ partition trace of reading (i).

**(c) The equilibrium assumption and thermal means.** The model **assumes**
that, for a declared sample of the species at the assigned temperature $T$
and in the absence of further preparation information, the preparation
description of the sample is $\rho_\beta$ in the sense of P1. For an assigned
sharp observable $(A,u_A)$ with spectral PVM $E_A$, define its outcome law
$\mu_{\rho_\beta}^A(B):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta E_A(B))$ as in
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b).
If and only if the absolute first moment is finite,
$$\int_{\mathbb R}|a|\,d\mu_{\rho_\beta}^A(a)<\infty,$$
the model defines the **thermal mean** at temperature $T$ by
$$\langle A\rangle_\beta:=\int_{\mathbb R}a\,d\mu_{\rho_\beta}^A(a),$$
read in the assigned unit $u_A$. For bounded $A$ this equals
$\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta A)=\operatorname{tr}(A\rho_\beta)$. For
unbounded $A$, if the mean exists and the literal product $A\rho_\beta$ is
defined on the whole Hilbert space and is trace class, the mean also equals
$\operatorname{tr}(A\rho_\beta)$ and
$\operatorname{tr}(\overline{\rho_\beta A})$; these conditional product
identities are proved by the density eigenexpansion in
[[lem-nrqm-many-body-spectral-mean-and-defined-trace-product]]. First-moment
existence alone imposes no such product or operator-square-domain condition.
When the absolute first moment is infinite the model asserts no finite
thermal mean. The identification of the parameter $T$ with the thermodynamic temperature of a
sample, and of $\beta$ with its inverse temperature, is part of this
assumption; the stated conservation and equilibrium properties of
$\rho_\beta$ under the flow of P4, and the extremal property of $\rho_\beta$
among preparations, are separate conditional results of this pair.

**(d) Motivation and status.** The assumption is motivated, but not
established, by the maximum-entropy reasoning of the cited sources: among
preparations with a prescribed mean energy, the Gibbs weights maximize the
entropy functional, and the finite-dimensional comparison theorem makes
$\rho_\beta$ the minimizer of the corresponding functional built from $G$.
Its physical Helmholtz free-energy reading applies in the stated finite
fixed-sector class; an effective-generator interpretation in a different
mode model is a separate declared reading. That reasoning is
an argument inside mathematical statistics and thermodynamics; it does not
derive the physical assumption that a sample is described by $\rho_\beta$.
The postulate is an **adopted** statistical-mechanical assumption of the
model, in the sense of the content model's distinction between adopted
assumptions and derived consequences.

**(e) Scope.** The postulate asserts nothing about how a sample reaches the
Gibbs preparation; in particular it asserts no thermalization, no equilibration
time, no ergodicity, no master-equation or Markov approximation, no
thermodynamic limit, no pressure, volume or phase-transition structure, and
no measured temperature or expectation. The requirement $0<Z<\infty$ is part
of the assumption; the model does not define a canonical preparation when
$Z=0$ or the partition trace diverges. Any comparison with a laboratory sample requires the
declared preparation, isolation, detection and sampling models of P7, and
agreement of a thermal prediction with data is evidence about the combined
model and apparatus assumptions, not a proof of the framework or of this
postulate.

Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 6.4 printed pages 129-131 (PDF pages 137-139): the maximum-entropy motivation, the Gibbs distribution rho = Z^{-1} sum e^{-beta E_i}|i><i| (6.94), beta = 1/(k_B T) and Z = sum e^{-beta E_i} (6.93a,b), U = Tr(H rho) (6.95) and S = k_B s (6.98)

I. Burmistrov and A.
