items.physical_scope: The adopted equilibrium-ensemble assumption of the many-body pair: for a declared fixed-N model or a separately declared number-variable mode model with self-adjoint semibounded Gibbs generator G (including a declared effective generator H-mu N), assigned temperature and strictly positive finite partition trace, the Gibbs preparation rho_beta = e^{-beta G}/Z, its thermal means, and the identifications of beta = 1/(k_B T) and of rho_beta with the model's description of thermal equilibrium. It is an adopted statistical-mechanical assumption motivated by maximum-entropy reasoning, not a consequence of the framework's state, probability or dynamics postulates; it asserts no thermalization, no equilibration rate, no thermodynamic limit and no fact about a laboratory sample except through the tested identifications of P7.

items.title: Diagonalisation of the non-interacting finite-mode sector: occupation eigenvalues, partition sum and ground energy
items.statement:
Adopt the state and composition postulate P1
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]]), the observable and
probability postulate P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]),
the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4
([[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]) and the identical-particle and
spin postulate P6 ([[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]) in
the readings of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]]
and [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and assume
the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Work in the
finite-mode realization of the declared fixed-$N$ model of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-declared-fixed-n-model]]: one-particle space
$K$ of finite dimension $d\ge1$ with declared modes $(f_1,\dots,f_d)$,
particle number $N\ge1$, sector space
$\mathfrak H_N^\sigma=\operatorname{ran}P_\sigma^{(N)}$, one-particle
self-adjoint operator $h\in\mathcal B(K)$, and **non-interacting** interaction
$W=0$, so that $H_{\mathrm{lab}}=\sum_{i=1}^Nh^{(i)}$ and
$H_N^\sigma=H_{\mathrm{lab}}|_{\mathfrak H_N^\sigma}$ in the notation of that
definition. Let $e_1,\dots,e_d$ be an orthonormal basis of eigenvectors of
$h$ with real eigenvalues $\varepsilon_1,\dots,\varepsilon_d$ and let
$\varepsilon_{(1)}\le\cdots\le\varepsilon_{(d)}$ be the nondecreasing
rearrangement of the list. Then:

(a) *the labelled operator is diagonal*: $H_{\mathrm{lab}}$ is bounded and
self-adjoint with $\|H_{\mathrm{lab}}\|\le N\|h\|$, it commutes with every
permutation unitary $U_\pi$, and for every multi-index
$i=(i_1,\dots,i_N)\in\{1,\dots,d\}^N$,
$$H_{\mathrm{lab}}\,(e_{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{i_N})=\Bigl(\sum_{k=1}^N\varepsilon_{i_k}\Bigr)e_{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{i_N};$$

(b) *occupation eigenvalues and spectrum*: for every $N$-element subset
$J\subseteq\{1,\dots,d\}$ the Slater vector $e_J^\wedge$ of
[[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-occupation-number-basis]] clause (b) is an
eigenvector of $H_N^-$ with eigenvalue $\lambda_J:=\sum_{j\in J}\varepsilon_j$,
and for every occupation vector $\lambda\in W(N,d)=\{\lambda\in\mathbb N^d:\sum_j\lambda_j=N\}$
the symmetric vector $m_\lambda$ of clause (c) is an eigenvector of
$H_N^+$ with eigenvalue $\lambda_\lambda:=\sum_{j=1}^d\lambda_j\varepsilon_j$;
the families $(e_J^\wedge)$ and $(m_\lambda)$ are orthogonal bases of
$\mathfrak H_N^-$ and $\mathfrak H_N^+$ respectively, so the spectrum of
$H_N^\sigma$ is the finite set of these eigenvalues (with multiplicities
given by the number of configurations producing them); for $\sigma=-$ and
$N>d$ the sector space is $\{0\}$ and the model has no sector states;

(c) *partition sum and ground energy*: write
$$\mathcal C_N^\sigma:=\{\lambda\in W(N,d):\lambda_j\le1\ \text{for every }j\ \text{if }\sigma=-\},\qquad M_N^\sigma:=|\mathcal C_N^\sigma|=\dim\mathfrak H_N^\sigma.$$
The configuration counts are $M_N^- =\binom dN$ and
$M_N^+ =\binom{N+d-1}{N}$. For every inverse-energy parameter
$\beta>0$ in $\mathrm J^{-1}$ (all $\varepsilon_j$ and configuration
energies are read in joules, so each Boltzmann exponent is dimensionless),
$$Z_N(\beta):=\operatorname{tr}e^{-\beta H_N^\sigma}=\sum_{\lambda\in\mathcal C_N^\sigma}e^{-\beta\lambda_\lambda}$$
is finite. If $\sigma=-$ and $N>d$, then $\mathcal C_N^-=\varnothing$,
$Z_N(\beta)=0$, and there is no ground eigenvalue or trace-one density
operator on the zero sector; in particular no normalized Gibbs density can
be formed there. Otherwise $M_N^\sigma>0$ and $0<Z_N(\beta)<\infty$.
In this nonzero-sector case, let
$$E_0:=\min_{\lambda\in\mathcal C_N^\sigma}\lambda_\lambda,\qquad E_{\max}:=\max_{\lambda\in\mathcal C_N^\sigma}\lambda_\lambda.$$
Then the actual Boltzmann bounds are
$$M_N^\sigma e^{-\beta E_{\max}}\le Z_N(\beta)\le M_N^\sigma e^{-\beta E_0}.$$
No nonnegativity hypothesis on the $\varepsilon_j$ is imposed. For
$\sigma=-$ and $N\le d$,
$$E_0=\sum_{k=1}^N\varepsilon_{(k)},\qquad E_{\max}=\sum_{k=d-N+1}^d\varepsilon_{(k)},$$
and for $\sigma=+$,
$$E_0=N\varepsilon_{(1)},\qquad E_{\max}=N\varepsilon_{(d)}.$$
For every unit vector $\psi\in\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$ in either nonzero sector,
$\langle H_N^\sigma\psi,\psi\rangle\ge E_0$, with equality exactly on the
eigenspace of $E_0$;

(d) *reading and stationarity*: on a nonzero sector the pair $(H_N^\sigma,\mathrm J)$ is the
model's assigned energy observable; in a declared sector preparation $\rho$
its outcome law is $\mu_\rho(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_{H_N^\sigma}(B))$,
and in the pure preparation of each sector basis vector of clause (b) this
law is the point mass at the displayed eigenvalue; each such vector is a
stationary state of the model evolution $U(t)=\exp(-itH_N^\sigma/\hbar)$, and
the energy law of every declared sector preparation is the law of the finite
spectral sum in the sector basis;

(e) *scope*: the theorem is conditional on the finite-mode idealization, on
the declared $h$ and on $W=0$; it asserts nothing for interacting models, for
spatial realizations, for infinite mode families, about thermal states or
equilibration, and about any laboratory system.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Sections 6.1 and 10.1 printed pages 104-111 and 226-230 (PDF pages 112-119 and 234-238): non-interacting composite Hamiltonians, antisymmetric two-fermion states and Pauli exclusion

F. H. L. Essler, Advanced Quantum Theory (Oxford lecture notes, 2017/18), Sections 1.2-1.3 pp. 5-9: the occupation-number basis and the diagonal form of a non-interacting many-body Hamiltonian in second quantisation

items.physical_scope: The conditional diagonalisation of the non-interacting finite-mode many-body model: the labelled energy sum is diagonal on the product basis of one-particle eigenmodes, the sector energy operator has the occupation-number eigenvalues on the Slater and symmetric sector bases, the finite partition sum and the ground-state occupation energies are computed, and the sector basis vectors are stationary states of the model evolution. The theorem is conditional on P1, P2, P4 and P6, on the adopted finite-mode idealization and on the declared one-particle Hamiltonian; it asserts no interaction, no spatial or infinite-mode result, no thermal state, no thermodynamic limit and no laboratory identification.

items.title: The one-body readout law: sector means of summed bounded one-particle quantities and their reduced forms
items.statement:
**Slot convention.** For $\ell\ge1$, $S_\ell$ acts on $\{0,\dots,\ell-1\}$ as in [[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]. On one-based tuple positions use $\widehat{\pi}(k):=1+\pi(k-1)$ for $1\le k\le\ell$. Conjugation by $k\mapsto k-1$ gives $\widehat{\pi\sigma}=\widehat{\pi}\circ\widehat{\sigma}$ and $\widehat{\pi^{-1}}=\widehat{\pi}^{-1}$; thus the supplier's tensor action becomes $U_\pi(v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_\ell)=v_{\widehat{\pi}^{-1}(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{\widehat{\pi}^{-1}(\ell)}$. The parameters of $U_\pi$ and $\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)$ remain canonical zero-based permutations.

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]]), the observable and
probability postulate P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]])
and the identical-particle and spin postulate P6
([[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]) in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]]
and [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and assume
the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]) as the choice hypotheses
of the cited tensor, permutation and trace suppliers. Work in the finite-mode
realization of [[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-one-body-reduced-operator]]:
one-particle space $K$ of finite dimension $d\ge1$ with modes
$(f_1,\dots,f_d)$, integer $N\ge1$ with nonzero sector space
$\mathfrak H_N^\sigma=\operatorname{ran}P_\sigma^{(N)}$, and the slot
operators $O^{(i)}$, sum $\Sigma(O)$ and one-body reduced preparation
$\gamma_\rho$ of that definition. Let $O\in\mathcal B(K)$ be self-adjoint
with declared unit $u_O$ in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Then:

(a) *the readout is an assigned observable*: the sector operator
$A_O=\Sigma(O)|_{\mathfrak H_N^\sigma}$ is bounded and self-adjoint, so the
pair $(A_O,u_O)$ is an assigned sharp observable of the sector in the sense
of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a);

(b) *the mean law*: for every declared sector preparation $\rho$ the mean of
the outcome law of $(A_O,u_O)$ in $\rho$ exists and equals
$$m_\rho(A_O)=N\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\gamma_\rho\,O\bigr);$$

(c) *product-type preparations*: let $u_1,\dots,u_N\in K$ be pairwise orthonormal. For $\sigma=-$ and $N\ge2$, let $\Psi:=S(u_1,\dots,u_N)$ be the Slater vector of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-slater-direct-and-exchange-calculation]] clause (a); for $\sigma=-$ and $N=1$, put $S(u_1):=u_1$ and $\Psi:=u_1$. For $\sigma=+$, put $\Psi:=\sqrt{N!}\,P_+^{(N)}(u_1\otimes\cdots\otimes u_N)$. In either case $\Psi$ is a unit vector of the sector. For $\rho:=T_{\Psi,\Psi}$ one has $\gamma_\rho=N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^NT_{u_j,u_j}$ and
$$m_\rho(A_O)=\sum_{j=1}^N\langle Ou_j,u_j\rangle.$$

(d) *scope*: the theorem is conditional on the adopted sector of P6, on the
declared finite-mode idealization and on the declared preparation; it asserts
no measured mean, no property of an individual labelled particle, no
separability of $\rho$, no result for spatial infinite-mode models, and no
sampling or detection model. The equality $m_\rho(A_O)=N\operatorname{tr}(\gamma_\rho O)$
is exact within the model.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Sections 6.2-6.3 and 10.1 printed pages 116-126 and 226-230 (PDF pages 124-134 and 234-238): local operators on a composite system, the reduced density operator of one factor, and identical-particle exchange symmetry with the two-particle example

F. H. L. Essler, Advanced Quantum Theory (Oxford lecture notes, 2017/18), Section 1.4.2 pp. 8-10: single-particle operators as sums over particle labels (46)-(48) and their second-quantised form (49)-(52)

items.physical_scope: The conditional one-body readout law of the declared finite-mode many-body model: for a bounded self-adjoint one-particle quantity the summed sector operator is an assigned sharp observable, its mean in every declared sector preparation exists and is N times the pairing of the one-body reduced preparation with the quantity, and for declared Slater and orthonormal-mode symmetric preparations the reduced preparation is the equal-weight mixture of the occupied modes. The theorem is conditional on P1, P2 and P6, the adopted finite-mode idealization and the declared preparation; it asserts no measured mean, no individual-particle property, no separability of the sector state and no spatial (infinite-mode) reduction.

items.title: Direct and exchange contributions to a two-fermion mean energy and the repulsive-Coulomb ordering
items.statement:
Adopt the state and composition postulate P1
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]]), the observable and
probability postulate P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]),
the non-relativistic kinematics postulate P5
([[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]]) and
the identical-particle and spin postulate P6
([[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]) in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and
[[pthm-nrqm-observables-preparation-moments]], and assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Take a declared spin-$\tfrac12$ fermionic species
with mass $m>0$, the spatial realization of the declared fixed-$N$ model of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-declared-fixed-n-model]] with $N=2$, a
bounded real external potential $V_{\mathrm{ext}}$ and one of the following
two pair interactions: (bounded case) a bounded real even
$W:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$; (Coulomb case) $W(z)=\kappa/|z|$ with
$\kappa>0$ and $V_{\mathrm{ext}}$ bounded. Let $u,v\in W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$
be pairwise orthonormal spatial orbitals, put
$$\varepsilon_u:=\langle h u,u\rangle_\star,\qquad \varepsilon_v:=\langle h v,v\rangle_\star$$
with $h=-\hbar^2\Delta/(2m)+V_{\mathrm{ext}}$ the declared one-particle operator and $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_\star$
the $L^2(\mathbb R^3)$ pairing, and let $D$ and $X$ be the direct and
exchange integrals
$$D=\int_{\mathbb R^6}|u(x)|^2|v(y)|^2W(x-y)\,dx\,dy,\qquad X=\int_{\mathbb R^6}\overline{u(x)}v(x)u(y)\overline{v(y)}\,W(x-y)\,dx\,dy$$
of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-slater-direct-and-exchange-calculation]]
clauses (c),(d), as appropriate. Fix the standard orthonormal basis $e_\uparrow,e_\downarrow$ of the declared spin-$\tfrac12$ factor $\mathbb C^2$, and define the unit spin vectors
$$\chi_-=(e_\uparrow\otimes e_\downarrow-e_\downarrow\otimes e_\uparrow)/\sqrt2,\qquad \chi_+=(e_\uparrow\otimes e_\downarrow+e_\downarrow\otimes e_\uparrow)/\sqrt2,$$
read as the singlet and symmetric $S_z=0$ triplet of the declared basis. Let $\Theta_{\mathrm{sp}}$ be the scalar Euclidean product unitary and let
$$\Theta_2:(L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^2))^{\otimes2}\longrightarrow L^2(\mathbb R^6;\mathbb C^2\otimes\mathbb C^2)$$
be the full spin-product unitary of [[lem-nrqm-many-body-finite-spin-product-identification]] clause (a). Put
$$\varphi_\pm=(u\otimes v\pm v\otimes u)/\sqrt2,\qquad f_\pm=\Theta_{\mathrm{sp}}\varphi_\pm,\qquad \Phi_\pm=\Theta_2^{-1}(f_\pm\chi_\mp),\qquad \rho_\pm=T_{\Phi_\pm,\Phi_\pm}.$$
Thus $\Phi_\pm$ are vectors in the declared one-particle tensor square, not untransported vectors in a regrouped spatial/spin product. They define the two declared preparations after the sector membership proved below. No reality assumption is imposed on the complex orbitals $u,v$.

(a) *declared preparations*: $\Phi_\pm$ are unit vectors of the antisymmetric
sector $\mathfrak H_2^-$ of the model, and $\rho_\pm$ are declared sector
preparations;

(b) *mean energies*: the means of the declared energy observable in the two
preparations exist, are finite and equal
$$m_{\rho_+}(H_2^-)=\varepsilon_u+\varepsilon_v+D+X,\qquad m_{\rho_-}(H_2^-)=\varepsilon_u+\varepsilon_v+D-X;$$
in particular the **exchange splitting** of the two preparations is
$m_{\rho_+}-m_{\rho_-}=2X$;

(c) *repulsive-Coulomb ordering*: in the Coulomb case with $u,v\in W^{1,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$
one has $X\ge0$ and therefore $m_{\rho_-}(H_2^-)\le m_{\rho_+}(H_2^-)$: the
spatially antisymmetric, spin-triplet preparation has the lower mean pair
energy of the two;

(d) *scope*: clauses (a)-(c) are conditional consequences of the declared
model, the declared orbitals and the adopted spin-statistics sector of P6;
they derive no spin-statistics theorem, assert no measured energy difference,
compare no experimental spectrum, and make no claim that the declared
orbitals approximate any atomic state.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Sections 10.1-10.2 printed pages 229-235 (PDF pages 237-243): the symmetric and antisymmetric electron-pair spatial functions, the direct and exchange integrals D and E of the pair interaction, the singlet-triplet ordering and the perturbative helium estimates

R. Fitzpatrick, Quantum Mechanics (University of Texas at Austin, author-hosted course text), Chapter 6 'Multi-Particle Systems', Sections 6.4-6.5 printed pages 88-92 (PDF pages 87-91): two-particle systems with the centre-of-mass and reduced-mass separation, the symmetry requirement on identical-particle wavefunctions and the overlap-dependent exchange correction to the pair probability

items.physical_scope: The conditional two-fermion exchange computation of the declared N=2 bounded or Coulomb model: for a declared pair of orthonormal spatial orbitals and the two declared antisymmetric sector preparations obtained by combining them with the spin singlet and triplet, the mean pair energies are the sum of the one-body means plus the direct integral and minus or plus the exchange integral, and for a repulsive Coulomb pair interaction the spatially antisymmetric (spin-triplet) preparation has the lower mean energy. The comparison is a statement about the declared model's means; it derives no spin-statistics assignment, reports no measured level splitting and makes no claim about a real atom.

items.title: The canonical preparation as the unique free-energy minimiser of the declared finite-sector model
items.statement:
Adopt the canonical equilibrium-ensemble postulate
[[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]] together with the
state, probability, dynamics and preparation postulates P1, P2, P4, P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]) in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]] and
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and assume the
Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Work in the
finite-dimensional sector class of the entropy definition: the declared
fixed-$N$ model of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-declared-fixed-n-model]] has sector space
$\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$ of finite dimension $D\ge1$ with self-adjoint energy
operator $H_N^\sigma$, assigned temperature $T>0$, inverse temperature
$\beta=1/(k_BT)$ and eigen-decomposition
$H_N^\sigma=\sum_{j=1}^DE_jT_{v_j,v_j}$ with orthonormal eigenbasis
$(v_1,\dots,v_D)$ and real eigenvalues $E_1,\dots,E_D$. Write
$q_j:=e^{-\beta E_j}/Z_N$ with $Z_N:=\sum_je^{-\beta E_j}$,
$\rho_\beta:=\sum_jq_jT_{v_j,v_j}$, and let
$F(\rho)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho H_N^\sigma)-k_BT\,s(\rho)$ and
$F_{\mathrm{eq}}:=-k_BT\log Z_N$ be the free-energy functional and
equilibrium free energy of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]] clauses (e).
Then:

(a) *the canonical preparation*: $Z_N\in(0,\infty)$ is a finite sum,
$q_j>0$, $\sum_jq_j=1$, and $\rho_\beta$ is a declared sector preparation of
the model with
$$\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H_N^\sigma)=\frac1{Z_N}\sum_{j=1}^DE_je^{-\beta E_j},\qquad s(\rho_\beta)=\log Z_N+\beta\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H_N^\sigma);$$

(b) *free-energy minimum*: for every declared sector preparation $\rho$ one
has $F(\rho)\ge F_{\mathrm{eq}}=-k_BT\log Z_N$;

(c) *uniqueness*: equality $F(\rho)=F_{\mathrm{eq}}$ holds if and only if
$\rho=\rho_\beta$; consequently the canonical preparation is the unique
minimiser of the free-energy functional over the declared sector
preparations, and $F(\rho_\beta)=F_{\mathrm{eq}}$;

(d) *degenerate case*: if $H_N^\sigma=c\,\mathrm{id}$ for a real $c$, then
$Z_N=De^{-\beta c}$, $\rho_\beta=D^{-1}\mathrm{id}$,
$s(\rho_\beta)=\log D$ and $F_{\mathrm{eq}}=c-k_BT\log D$;

(e) *scope*: the statement is conditional on the adopted ensemble postulate
and on the declared finite-dimensional model; it asserts no equilibration of
any preparation towards $\rho_\beta$, no rate of approach, no thermodynamic
limit, no pressure or volume variable, and, for a laboratory sample, it
inherits the tested identification of the preparation and temperature
assignment of P7.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 6.4 printed pages 129-131 (PDF pages 137-139): the Gibbs distribution as the maximum-entropy distribution for given internal energy, U = Tr(H rho), s = beta U + ln Z (6.97), S = k_B s (6.98) and F = -k_B T ln Z (6.99)

I. Burmistrov and A. Lunkin, Lecture Notes on Statistical Mechanics (HSE, January 10, 2023), Section 1.1.4 printed pages 14-15: the maximal-entropy derivation of the Gibbs distribution, the free energy F = -T ln Z and the relations F = E - T S, S = -dF/dT

items.physical_scope: The conditional free-energy characterisation of the canonical preparation in the declared finite-sector many-body model at assigned temperature: the Gibbs operator is a declared preparation, its mean energy and entropy are the finite Gibbs sums, and it is the unique minimiser of the free-energy functional over all declared sector preparations, the minimum being the equilibrium free energy. The theorem is conditional on the adopted ensemble postulate and the declared model; it asserts no equilibration, no approach to equilibrium, no thermodynamic limit and no measured thermal quantity.

items.title: Thermal occupation means of the declared free-mode models: Bose and Fermi factors, product convergence and dilute remainders
items.statement:
Adopt the canonical equilibrium-ensemble postulate
[[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]] for the mode models
declared below, the state and probability postulates P1, P2
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]) in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and
[[pthm-nrqm-observables-preparation-moments]], and the
identical-particle and spin postulate P6
([[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]); assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Temperatures are assigned as in
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]], so that
$\beta=1/(k_BT)$ in $\mathrm J^{-1}$. Declare the occupation readouts as assigned sharp observables $(N,1)$ and $(N_-,1)$, with unit particle-count, which is dimensionless. The total particle-number operator $\mathcal N$ in the countable-mode reading has the same unit; every occupation mean and higher number moment below is read in the corresponding dimensionless count unit. Then:

(a) *single bosonic mode*: let $F(\mathbb C)$ be the one-mode Fock space with
number operator $N$ and orthonormal number basis $(e_n)$
([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fixed-mode-number-law]],
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-number-operator-domain]]), let
$\varepsilon>0$ and let the model declare the energy operator $H:=\varepsilon N$
on $F(\mathbb C)$; the model's canonical preparation at temperature $T$ is
$\rho_\beta=e^{-\beta H}/Z$ with $Z=(1-e^{-\beta\varepsilon})^{-1}$, the
number readout $N$ is an assigned sharp observable with finite thermal mean
$$\langle N\rangle_\beta=\frac1{e^{\beta\varepsilon}-1}=\frac1{e^{\varepsilon/(k_BT)}-1},$$
and all moments $\langle N^k\rangle_\beta$, $k\ge1$, are finite;

(b) *single fermionic orbital and grand-canonical shift*: on
$\mathfrak h=\mathbb C^2$ with occupation operator $N_-$ and
$\varepsilon_1,\mu\in\mathbb R$, the model's canonical (grand-canonical)
preparation $F=Z^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^1e^{-\beta(\varepsilon_1-\mu)k}T_{u_k,u_k}$
has $Z=1+e^{-\beta(\varepsilon_1-\mu)}$, $\operatorname{tr}F=1$, and occupation mean
$$\langle N_-\rangle=\frac1{e^{\beta(\varepsilon_1-\mu)}+1};$$
the same formula is the model's thermal mean when $\mu=0$ and
$\varepsilon_1>0$;

(c) *countably many independent modes*: let $(\varepsilon_j)_{j\ge1}\subseteq(0,\infty)$
and $\mu\in\mathbb R$, and let the model declare the free-mode energies
$\varepsilon_j$ (one mode case of clause (a)) with the product reading of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-countable-mode-product-criterion]]; then the
bosonic product partition is finite exactly when
$\sum_je^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}<\infty$ and $\mu<\inf_j\varepsilon_j$, and
the fermionic product partition is finite exactly when
$\sum_je^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}<\infty$; in the finite cases the products
equal $\prod_j(1-e^{-\beta(\varepsilon_j-\mu)})^{-1}$ and
$\prod_j(1+e^{-\beta(\varepsilon_j-\mu)})$ respectively;

(d) *dilute remainders*: for $q=e^{-\beta(\varepsilon-\mu)}$ the model's
occupation means satisfy the exact identities
$$\frac q{1-q}=q+\frac{q^2}{1-q}\quad(\text{bosonic},\ 0<q<1),\qquad \frac q{1+q}=q-\frac{q^2}{1+q}\quad(\text{fermionic},\ q>0),$$
so both differ from $q$ by at most $q^2/(1-q)$ and $q^2/(1+q)$
respectively;

(e) *scope*: clauses (a)-(d) are conditional statements about the declared
mode models together with the adopted ensemble assignment; they assert no
thermodynamic limit, no continuum of radiation modes, no Bose-Einstein
condensation, no measured occupation number, and no thermalisation of a
sample. All numerical equalities are exact identities of the declared
finite-mode (or product) models at the assigned temperature.

references.title: I. Burmistrov and A. Lunkin, Lecture Notes on Statistical Mechanics (HSE, January 10, 2023), Section 1.3.1 printed pages 24-27: the single-level and many-level grand-canonical partition functions for fermions and the Fermi-Dirac distribution; Section 1.4.1 printed pages 33-34: the geometric sums for one bosonic level and the Bose-Einstein distribution; Section 1.4.2 printed page 34: the canonical partition function for N bosons

J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 10.1 printed pages 226-230 (PDF pages 234-238): single-particle states of a species and the counting of antisymmetric and symmetric configurations underlying the mode occupations

items.physical_scope: The declared free-mode thermal models of the pair: a single bosonic mode with energy operator epsilon N on the one-mode Fock space, a single fermionic orbital with two-dimensional occupation space and grand-canonical shift, and countably many independent modes with positive energies, each equipped with the adopted canonical preparation at assigned temperature. The theorem records the model's thermal occupation means, the partition-product convergence criterion and the dilute remainders; it asserts no thermodynamic limit, no continuum density of states, no Bose-Einstein condensation, no measured occupation and no thermalisation of any sample.

items.title: Unitary evolution preserves entropy and cannot produce the canonical preparation from a different one
items.statement:
Adopt the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4
([[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]) in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]], the state postulate P1
and the observable postulate P2
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]) in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-declared-fixed-n-model]] and
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]], and adopt the
canonical equilibrium-ensemble postulate
[[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]] for the canonical
preparation $\rho_\beta$; assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom
of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Work in the
finite-sector class of the entropy definition: the declared model has
finite-dimensional sector space $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$, self-adjoint energy
operator $H_N^\sigma$ with flow
$U(t)=\exp(-itH_N^\sigma/\hbar)$, and every declared sector preparation
evolves as $\rho(t)=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^*$ under P4 clause (iii). Then:

(a) *entropy is conserved*: for every declared sector preparation $\rho(0)$
of the model and every $t\in\mathbb R$,
$$s(\rho(t))=s(\rho(0));$$

(b) *the canonical preparation is stationary*:
$U(t)\rho_\beta U(t)^*=\rho_\beta$ for every $t$, and every thermal mean
$\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta A)$ of an assigned observable is time
independent;

(c) *no unitary production of the canonical preparation*: if
$\rho(0)\ne\rho_\beta$ then $\rho(t)\ne\rho_\beta$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$;
equivalently, no evolution of this isolated model maps a non-canonical
declared preparation to the canonical one at any time;

(d) *scope*: clauses (a)-(c) concern the model's exact unitary flow in the
finite-sector class and the adopted canonical preparation. They assert
nothing about open systems or environment coupling, about the time behaviour
of individual readouts or their time averages, about an approach of any
readout to a thermal value in a limit, about environments or measurement
models, and about any laboratory sample; in particular clause (c) is not a
claim that no physical system ever approaches thermal equilibrium, but the
statement that the model's P4 dynamics alone does not do so.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Sections 6.3-6.4 printed pages 122-131 (PDF pages 130-139): unitary evolution of the density operator, rho(t) = U rho U*, and the Gibbs distribution as the equilibrium density operator

I. Burmistrov and A. Lunkin, Lecture Notes on Statistical Mechanics (HSE, January 10, 2023), Section 1.1.1 printed page 12: the Liouville equation, its stationary solutions commuting with H, and the remark that the von Neumann entropy is conserved under the Liouville dynamics

items.physical_scope: The conditional conservation statement of the declared finite-sector model: under the unitary flow of the model's self-adjoint energy operator, every declared sector preparation keeps its entropy, the adopted canonical preparation is stationary, and a preparation different from it is never mapped to it at any time, so the model's unitary dynamics alone does not produce the canonical preparation. The theorem is about the exact closed-system model and asserts nothing about open systems, about equilibration of individual readouts, about time averages, or about any laboratory sample.

items.title: Scope and empirical status of the many-body and equilibrium models
items.statement:
## Recorded scope

The page declares and works with the finite-mode and spatial realizations of a
**declared fixed-$N$ many-body model**
([[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-declared-fixed-n-model]]): a species sector of
P6, a one-particle energy operator, a pair interaction and the self-adjoint
restriction of the labelled Hamiltonian to the adopted symmetric or
antisymmetric sector. The page also treats separately declared
number-variable free-mode spaces, including the one-mode and countable-mode
occupation models of [[pthm-nrqm-many-body-thermal-occupation-predictions]],
under reading (a)(ii) of
[[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]]; these are additional
model declarations, not realizations supplied by the fixed-$N$ definition.
Every result is conditional on its own stated model and parameters:

- the non-interacting finite-mode model is diagonal in the occupation basis
  with the stated occupation eigenvalues, partition sum and ground energy
  ([[pthm-nrqm-many-body-noninteracting-sector-diagonalization]]);
- the one-body readout of a bounded self-adjoint one-particle quantity has
  mean equal to $N$ times the pairing of the one-body reduced preparation
  with that quantity ([[pthm-nrqm-many-body-one-body-readout-law]]);
- for two orthonormal orbitals satisfying the stated regularity and a repulsive
  Coulomb pair interaction, the spatially antisymmetric (spin-triplet) sector
  preparation has mean pair energy $D-X$, no greater than the spatially symmetric
  (spin-singlet) preparation's $D+X$, where $D$ and $X\ge0$ are the direct and
  exchange integrals of the cited theorem; the splitting is $2X$, and the
  triplet's mean pair energy is strictly lower exactly when $X>0$
  ([[pthm-nrqm-many-body-exchange-energy-splitting]]);
- in the finite-sector class the canonical preparation is the unique
  minimiser of the free-energy functional at the assigned
  $\beta=1/(k_BT)$ ([[pthm-nrqm-many-body-thermal-equilibrium-characterization]]);
- in the separately declared number-variable mode models, the free-mode
  thermal occupation means are the Bose and Fermi factors
  with the stated product convergence criterion and dilute remainders
  ([[pthm-nrqm-many-body-thermal-occupation-predictions]]);
- in the finite-sector class, the model's unitary flow preserves the entropy
  of every declared sector preparation and never maps a preparation different from the canonical one
  to it ([[pthm-nrqm-many-body-unitary-evolution-preserves-entropy]]).

## Adopted assumptions and parameters

The **canonical ensemble** is the adopted assumption of
[[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]]; the maximum-entropy
and free-energy arguments are motivations inside the model, and the
free-energy minimum theorem is a statement about the functional, not a
derivation of the ensemble from P1-P4. The **Boltzmann constant** is the exact
SI defining constant, while the **temperature**, **chemical potential**,
masses, couplings and any potential parameters are assigned model parameters
with uncertainty ([[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]],
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]). The assignment of a concrete
sample, mode family or detector to these model objects is a tested
identification under P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]).

## Explicitly not asserted

The page does **not** assert: thermalization or equilibration of any
preparation (the opposite conservation statement is proved for the closed
model); a thermodynamic limit, pressure, volume, phase transitions or
condensation; entropy or free energy for infinite-dimensional sectors, for
which $\rho\log\rho$ need not be trace class; any spin-statistics theorem,
which remains the adopted sector assignment of P6; any experimental value,
count or measured level splitting. The mode models are declared
idealizations: a finitely many-mode or product-of-modes reading of a free
system, not a derivation from a spatial continuum model. The exchange
computation of the page compares two declared preparations of one model; it
does not claim that any atom's spectrum equals the difference computed.

## Source limits

The physical reading of the Gibbs distribution and of the relations among
$U$, $S$ and $F$ follows the treatments of Binney-Skinner and Burmistrov-Lunkin
at the indicated locators; both are textbook and lecture-note presentations
whose thermodynamic identifications are heuristic model assumptions rather
than mathematical derivations, and the present page therefore records them as
adopted assumptions. Burmistrov-Lunkin work with $\beta$ as a formal
inverse-energy parameter and set $k_B=1$ implicitly; the SI reading
$\beta=1/(k_BT)$ with the exact BIPM value of $k_B$ used here is our own
convention, not a claim made at their locators. No source supplies measured
temperature-dependent data for the declared mode models on this page, and no
experiment item is created from these sources.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 6.4 printed pages 129-132 (PDF pages 137-140): the Gibbs distribution taken as the maximum-entropy distribution, the thermodynamic interpretation of Z, U, S and F, and the authors' own caution that the dependence of Z on T and V can be computed for only very few Hamiltonians

I. Burmistrov and A. Lunkin, Lecture Notes on Statistical Mechanics (HSE, January 10, 2023), Section 1.1.3 printed page 14: the remark that the von Neumann entropy is conserved under the Liouville equation, and Section 1.1.4 printed pages 14-15: the maximal-entropy motivation for the Gibbs distribution

title: Qm Many Body And Equilibrium Models — Examples

items.title: The two-site bond model: exact canonical weights, mean energy, entropy and free energy of one particle on two sites
items.statement:
Adopt P1, P2, P4 and P7 in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]], and work in the
finite-mode realization of the declared fixed-$N$ model of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-declared-fixed-n-model]] with:
one-particle space $K=\mathbb C^2$, declared sites $|1\rangle,|2\rangle$ an
orthonormal basis of $K$, particle number $N=1$, single site-occupation
sector, and the declared one-particle operator (the **bond Hamiltonian**)
$$h:=-t\bigl(T_{|1\rangle,|2\rangle}+T_{|2\rangle,|1\rangle}\bigr),\qquad t>0\ \text{in joules}.$$
Adopt the canonical equilibrium postulate
[[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]] at assigned
temperature $T>0$ and inverse temperature $\beta=1/(k_BT)$, and read
$\varepsilon:=2t$ as the tunnelling splitting. Then:

(a) $h$ has the orthonormal eigenbasis
$$u_-:=\frac{|1\rangle+|2\rangle}{\sqrt2},\qquad u_+:=\frac{|1\rangle-|2\rangle}{\sqrt2},\qquad h u_\mp=\mp t\,u_\mp,$$
so its eigenvalues are $-t$ and $+t$; equivalently $h+t\,\mathrm{id}$ is the
two-level Hamiltonian of
[[lem-nrqm-many-body-two-level-thermal-formulas]] with levels $0$ and
$\varepsilon=2t$ and eigenvectors $u_-,u_+$;

(b) the canonical preparation of $h+t\,\mathrm{id}$ and hence of $h$ is
$$\rho_\beta=\frac{T_{u_-,u_-}+e^{-2\beta t}\,T_{u_+,u_+}}{1+e^{-2\beta t}},$$
with shifted partition sum $Z_0=1+e^{-2\beta t}$ and physical partition trace $Z_h=\operatorname{tr}e^{-\beta h}=e^{\beta t}Z_0$;

(c) the exact means, entropy and free energy are
$$\langle h\rangle_\beta=\frac{2t}{e^{2\beta t}+1}-t=-t\tanh(\beta t),\qquad s(\rho_\beta)=\log\bigl(1+e^{-2\beta t}\bigr)+\frac{2\beta te^{-2\beta t}}{1+e^{-2\beta t}},\qquad F=-\frac1\beta\log\bigl(1+e^{-2\beta t}\bigr)-t,$$
and for every $\beta>0$ one has $-t<\langle h\rangle_\beta<0$ and
$0\le s(\rho_\beta)<\log2$;

(d) *scope*: the computation is an exact statement about the declared
two-dimensional bond model at the assigned temperature; it identifies no
physical double-well or molecular system, asserts no measured splitting and
no transition, and the temperature assignment is the tested identification of
P7.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 5.2 printed pages 79-81 (PDF pages 87-89): the double square well, the even and odd parity combinations and their splitting, with the two-level thermal reading following Section 6.4 printed pages 129-131

I. Burmistrov and A. Lunkin, Lecture Notes on Statistical Mechanics (HSE, January 10, 2023), Section 1.1.2 printed page 13 and Section 1.1.5 printed page 15: the canonical partition function and free energy of a finite-level system

items.physical_scope: A finite exact computation in the declared one-particle two-site (bond) model of the finite-mode many-body realization: the hopping Hamiltonian on two sites, its two exact one-particle levels, the canonical preparation at assigned temperature, and the exact mean energy, entropy and free energy. The example is a model computation in a declared two-dimensional idealization; it asserts no physical molecule, no measured energy, no transition and no thermodynamic limit.

items.title: Finite-mode non-interacting thermal ensembles: two fermions in three modes and two bosons in two modes
items.statement:
Adopt P1, P2 and P6 in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-orbital-occupation-model]] and
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], work in the
finite-mode realization of the declared fixed-$N$ model of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-declared-fixed-n-model]], and adopt the
canonical equilibrium postulate
[[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]] at assigned
temperature $T>0$ with $\beta=1/(k_BT)$. Fix $\varepsilon>0$ in joules.

**Fermionic model.** One-particle space $K=\mathbb C^3$ with modes
$f_1,f_2,f_3$, fermionic statistics $\sigma=-$, $N=2$, and the declared
one-particle operator $h:=\varepsilon\,(0\cdot T_{f_1,f_1}+1\cdot T_{f_2,f_2}+2\cdot T_{f_3,f_3})$.

**Bosonic model.** One-particle space $K=\mathbb C^2$ with modes $g_1,g_2$,
bosonic statistics $\sigma=+$, $N=2$, and $h':=\varepsilon(0\cdot T_{g_1,g_1}+1\cdot T_{g_2,g_2})$.

Then:

(a) in the fermionic model the antisymmetric sector has orthonormal
eigenbasis $e_{\{1,2\}}^\wedge,e_{\{1,3\}}^\wedge,e_{\{2,3\}}^\wedge$ with
energies $\varepsilon,2\varepsilon,3\varepsilon$; the partition sum and the
exact occupation means are
$$Z_{\mathrm F}=e^{-\beta\varepsilon}+e^{-2\beta\varepsilon}+e^{-3\beta\varepsilon},$$
$$\langle N_1\rangle_\beta=\frac{e^{-\beta\varepsilon}+e^{-2\beta\varepsilon}}{Z_{\mathrm F}},\quad \langle N_2\rangle_\beta=\frac{e^{-\beta\varepsilon}+e^{-3\beta\varepsilon}}{Z_{\mathrm F}},\quad \langle N_3\rangle_\beta=\frac{e^{-2\beta\varepsilon}+e^{-3\beta\varepsilon}}{Z_{\mathrm F}},$$
with $\langle N_1+N_2+N_3\rangle_\beta=2$ and ground energy
$\varepsilon$ (configuration $\{1,2\}$);

(b) in the bosonic model the symmetric sector has orthogonal eigenbasis
$m_{(2,0)},m_{(1,1)},m_{(0,2)}$ with energies $0,\varepsilon,2\varepsilon$;
the partition sum and the exact occupation means are
$$Z_{\mathrm B}=1+e^{-\beta\varepsilon}+e^{-2\beta\varepsilon},\qquad \langle N_1\rangle_\beta=\frac{2+e^{-\beta\varepsilon}}{Z_{\mathrm B}},\qquad \langle N_2\rangle_\beta=\frac{e^{-\beta\varepsilon}+2e^{-2\beta\varepsilon}}{Z_{\mathrm B}},$$
with $\langle N_1+N_2\rangle_\beta=2$ and ground energy $0=N\varepsilon_1$;

(c) *scope*: the computations are exact statements about the declared
finite-mode models at the assigned temperature; they assert no physical
species, no measured occupation, no thermalisation and no thermodynamic
limit.

references.title: F. H. L. Essler, Advanced Quantum Theory (Oxford lecture notes, 2017/18), Sections 1.1-1.2 and 1.4 pp. 3-13: independent-particle eigenstates as tensor products, occupation-number configurations, Fock-space sectors and the second-quantised form of one-body operators
J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 10.1 printed pages 226-230 (PDF pages 234-238): counting of antisymmetric two-particle configurations and the exclusion rule

items.physical_scope: Two exact finite-mode thermal computations in the declared non-interacting model: the canonical partition sums, ground energies and occupation means of two spinless fermions in three modes with energies 0, epsilon, 2 epsilon, and of two spinless bosons in two modes with energies 0 and epsilon, at assigned temperature. The examples are model computations in declared finite-dimensional idealizations; they assert no physical particle species, no measured occupation and no thermodynamic limit.

items.title: Free-mode statistics at low occupation: exact dilute identities, a finite arithmetic check and two convergence examples
items.statement:
Adopt the mode models and thermal readings of
[[pthm-nrqm-many-body-thermal-occupation-predictions]] at assigned
temperature $T>0$ with $\beta=1/(k_BT)$. For a canonical single mode of
energy $\varepsilon>0$, put $x:=\beta\varepsilon>0$ and
$q:=e^{-x}\in(0,1)$. In the grand-canonical reading put
$x:=\beta(\varepsilon-\mu)$ and $q:=e^{-x}>0$; the bosonic formulas below
apply only when $\mu<\varepsilon$ (so $q<1$), while the fermionic formulas
hold for every $\mu\in\mathbb R$.
Then:

(a) the exact single-mode means and their dilute identities are
$$\langle N\rangle_{\mathrm B}=\frac{q}{1-q}=q+\frac{q^2}{1-q},\qquad \langle N\rangle_{\mathrm F}=\frac{q}{1+q}=q-\frac{q^2}{1+q},$$
so the bosonic mean exceeds $q$ by $q^2/(1-q)$ and the fermionic mean falls
below $q$ by $q^2/(1+q)$ exactly;

(b) at $q=1/10$ the exact means are $\langle N\rangle_{\mathrm B}=1/9$ and
$\langle N\rangle_{\mathrm F}=1/11$, and the exact identities
$1/9=1/10+1/90$ and $1/11=1/10-1/110$ verify the two remainder formulas;

(c) for the free-mode energies $\varepsilon_j=j\varepsilon$,
$j\ge1$, the sums $\sum_je^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}=e^{-\beta\varepsilon}/(1-e^{-\beta\varepsilon})$
converge, so the bosonic and fermionic product partitions are finite
(bosonic case with $\mu<\varepsilon$); for the constant energies
$\varepsilon_j\equiv\varepsilon$ the sum $\sum_je^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}=+\infty$
diverges, so both product partitions diverge;

(d) *scope*: the identities and the check are exact statements about the
declared mode models at the assigned temperature and, where stated, chemical
potential; no measured occupation, dilute gas, thermodynamic limit or
condensation is asserted.

references.title: I. Burmistrov and A. Lunkin, Lecture Notes on Statistical Mechanics (HSE, January 10, 2023), Sections 1.3.1 and 1.4.1 printed pages 24-27 and 33-34: the Fermi-Dirac and Bose-Einstein occupation factors and their low-occupation expansions

J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 10.1 printed pages 226-230 (PDF pages 234-238): counting of symmetric and antisymmetric mode configurations behind the two statistics

items.physical_scope: A finite check of the declared free-mode thermal occupation formulas at low occupation q = e^{-beta epsilon}: the exact Bose and Fermi means, their dilute remainders, an exact rational evaluation at q = 1/10, and the product convergence for linearly spaced and for constant free-mode energies. The example is a model computation at assigned temperature and chemical potential; it asserts no measured occupation, no dilute gas, no thermodynamic limit and no condensation.

items.title: A site-localised preparation of the two-site bond model never becomes canonical, and its readouts need not take their thermal means
items.statement:
Adopt P1, P2, P4 and P7 in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]], work in the
**two-site bond model** of
[[ex-nrqm-many-body-two-site-bond-thermal-ensemble]] with coupling $t>0$,
sites $|1\rangle,|2\rangle$, bond Hamiltonian
$h=-t(T_{|1\rangle,|2\rangle}+T_{|2\rangle,|1\rangle})$ and eigenbasis
$u_-=(|1\rangle+|2\rangle)/\sqrt2$, $u_+=(|1\rangle-|2\rangle)/\sqrt2$ with $hu_\mp=\mp tu_\mp$, and adopt
the canonical equilibrium postulate
[[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]] at assigned
temperature $T>0$, $\beta=1/(k_BT)$. Consider the hypothetical declared
preparation $\rho(0):=T_{|1\rangle,|1\rangle}$ (the particle localised at
site $1$) evolving by $\rho(\tau)=U(\tau)\rho(0)U(\tau)^*$ with
$U(\tau)=\exp(-i\tau h/\hbar)$. Then:

(a) $\rho(0)\ne\rho_\beta$, and for every $\tau\in\mathbb R$ one has
$\rho(\tau)\ne\rho_\beta$: the unitary evolution of the model never produces
the canonical preparation from this preparation;

(b) the site-$1$ occupation readout $(P_1,1)$ with $P_1:=T_{|1\rangle,|1\rangle}$, assigned in the dimensionless particle-count unit, has the
exact mean
$$\langle P_1\rangle(\tau)=\cos^2\!\Bigl(\frac{t\tau}{\hbar}\Bigr),$$
and $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta P_1)=1/2$; in particular
$\langle P_1\rangle(0)=1\ne1/2$, so at the initial time the readout does not
take its canonical mean;

(c) the energy readout $h$ has the constant mean
$\operatorname{tr}(\rho(\tau)h)=0$ for every $\tau$, while its canonical mean
is $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta h)=-t\tanh(\beta t)<0$; hence the energy
readout never takes its canonical thermal value;

(d) *scope and interpretation*: the scenario is a hypothetical,
exactly-solved model deduction in one declared preparation; it shows that
agreement or disagreement of individual readout means with their canonical
values is not convergence of the preparation to the canonical one, and that
the model's P4 dynamics does not produce the canonical ensemble. It asserts
no observed equilibration or non-equilibration of a sample, no measured
occupation or energy, and no claim about environments or open systems.

items.title: What the companion examples and the thought experiment establish
items.statement:
## Recorded scope

The companion items contain three conditional examples and one hypothetical
scenario in declared finite-mode or countable-mode models:

- [[ex-nrqm-many-body-two-site-bond-thermal-ensemble]] solves the one-particle
  two-site bond model exactly: the tunnelling-split eigenbasis, the canonical
  weights and the exact mean energy, entropy and free energy;
- [[ex-nrqm-many-body-finite-mode-noninteracting-thermal-ensemble]] evaluates
  the canonical partition sums and occupation means of two fermions in three
  modes and two bosons in two modes, with the total-occupation identity and
  ground energies checked against the page's diagonalisation theorem;
- [[ex-nrqm-many-body-gas-statistics-dilute-limits]] verifies the exact Bose
  and Fermi dilute identities, evaluated in exact rational arithmetic at
  $q=1/10$, and contrasts the finite product partition of linearly
  spaced mode energies with the divergent product of constant energies;
- [[texp-nrqm-many-body-two-site-no-thermalization]] shows, in one declared
  hypothetical preparation of the bond model, that the unitary evolution
  never produces the canonical preparation, that the site-occupation readout
  takes the canonical value $1/2$ at some times while differing from it at
  others, and that the energy readout never takes its canonical value.

## What they do not establish

None of these items contains measured data, a measured uncertainty, a
calibration, a sampling model or a detector model; all numbers are exact
model values in the declared finite-mode or countable-mode idealizations, and
the assignment of a physical system to any of these models is a tested
identification under P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]). In particular:

- the bond model is not any particular molecule, and its splitting $2t$ is an
  assigned parameter, not a measured spectroscopic value;
- the finite-mode examples are not ideal or interacting gases; they make no
  statement about a thermodynamic limit, pressure, condensation or a
  continuum of modes;
- the comparison of readout means with canonical values in the thought
  experiment is a statement about the declared preparation and the exact
  unitary flow; it is not evidence for or against thermalisation in nature,
  and the canonical ensemble remains the adopted assumption of
  [[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]];
- the thought experiment uses the no-unitary-production conclusion (c) of
  [[pthm-nrqm-many-body-unitary-evolution-preserves-entropy]]. The separate
  entropy-conservation conclusion (a) of that theorem concerns the same
  finite closed-system class but is not a premise of the readout calculation;
  neither conclusion forbids or asserts open-system or environment-induced
  behaviour.

## Source limits

The cited treatments supply the model formulas used here at the recorded
locators; they do not supply measured values for these particular finite-mode
or countable-mode models, and no source is used as an empirical premise on this page. Where a
comparison with data would be attempted, the preparation, isolation,
detection and sampling models plus the uncertainty of every assigned
parameter would have to be declared and carried through, as P7 requires.
